# Region protocol

<!-- Generated from contracts/protocol.json; DO NOT EDIT. -->

[한국어](protocol.ko.md).

This document defines the application manifest, routing, rendering, the requests and responses between a hyper server and the hyper browser code, and the two rendering modes. The server can render the first document as HTML (server-side rendering, SSR), or a static shell can render it in the browser (client-side rendering, CSR). Template syntax and rendering rules are defined by the template language; this document does not change them.

## Application manifest

- **HY-1** <a id="HY-1.1"></a> An application declares its structure in one JSON file, the manifest. <a id="HY-1.2"></a> Server and browser read the same manifest.

```json
{
  "layout": "layout.tpl",
  "title": "title.tpl",
  "regions": [
    { "name": "left", "template": "left.tpl", "uses": ["posts", "path"] },
    { "name": "content", "page": true }
  ],
  "routes": [
    { "name": "board.list", "path": "/board", "title": "Board", "template": "board/list.tpl", "regions": [{ "name": "rows", "template": "board/rows.tpl" }] },
    { "name": "board.create", "path": "/board/create", "title": "Write", "template": "board/create.tpl", "post": true },
    { "name": "board.show", "path": "/board/{id}", "title": "Post", "template": "board/show.tpl",
      "representations": [{ "type": "application/vnd.example.post+json", "parameters": { "version": ["1"] }, "methods": ["GET", "PUT"], "vary": ["Authorization"] }] }
  ]
}
```

- **HY-2** <a id="HY-2.1"></a> `regions` and `routes` are ordered lists. <a id="HY-2.2"></a> Region names and route names are strings and are unique. <a id="HY-2.3"></a> A region name matches `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and is not `layout`, `title`, `data` or `build`. <a id="HY-2.4"></a> Exactly one region has `"page": true` and no `template`; every other region has a `template` and a list of used topics. <a id="HY-2.5"></a> A route with `"post": true` accepts a `POST` action. <a id="HY-2.6"></a> A route may declare `representations` (HY-118). <a id="HY-2.7"></a> A server checks its manifest against these rules when it starts, and `hyper build` checks the manifest before it writes any output (HR-96); the browser does not check the manifest of its bundle again. <a id="HY-2.9"></a> The manifest file is JSON text as HY-54.20 reads it, so a text that json refuses, such as one with more than 256 nested containers, and a value outside the data model, such as one with a lone surrogate escape or deeper than 64 levels, fail the open with kind `invalid_application` (HY-106.21).

- **HY-3** <a id="HY-3.1"></a> The layout renders the title definition inside `<title>` with `{# title}`, the data definition with `{# data}` (HY-31), the build definition with `{# build}` inside `<head>` (HY-125), and each region with `{# name}` inside an element whose `id` is the region name, for example `<main id="content">{# content}</main>`. <a id="HY-3.2"></a> A region placement has no block arguments. <a id="HY-3.3"></a> The browser finds a region element by its `id`; no other marker exists.

## Routing

- **HY-4** <a id="HY-4.1"></a> A route path starts with `/`. <a id="HY-4.2"></a> The segments after it are separated by `/`. <a id="HY-4.3"></a> A segment is either a literal of the characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -` or a parameter `{name}` where `name` matches `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. <a id="HY-4.4"></a> The path `/` has no segments. <a id="HY-4.6"></a> The router refuses a route path against this rule or HY-49, such as one that repeats a parameter name, so an application whose manifest declares it fails to open.

- **HY-5** <a id="HY-5.1"></a> A request path matches a route when it starts with `/`, has the same number of segments, every literal segment is equal to the request segment byte for byte, and every parameter segment is non-empty. <a id="HY-5.2"></a> The query string is not part of the path. <a id="HY-5.3"></a> The parameters of a match are a map from each parameter name to its value, in the order of the parameters in the route path.

- **HY-6** <a id="HY-6.1"></a> A parameter value is the request segment with every `%XX` sequence (two hexadecimal digits) decoded to its byte. <a id="HY-6.2"></a> A segment with a `%` that is not followed by two hexadecimal digits, or whose decoded bytes are not valid UTF-8, does not match.

- **HY-7** <a id="HY-7.1"></a> Routes are tried in manifest order, and the first route that matches is the result. <a id="HY-7.2"></a> A path that matches no route has no result.

- **HY-8** <a id="HY-8.1"></a> An application may run under a base path such as `/api`. <a id="HY-8.2"></a> A request path is routed after removing the base path; a request path that does not start with the base path followed by `/` or the end of the path has no result. <a id="HY-8.3"></a> `Location` headers include the base path.

- **HY-49** <a id="HY-49.1"></a> The last segment of a route path may be a rest parameter `{name*}`, with `name` as in HY-4 and different from the other parameters of the path. <a id="HY-49.2"></a> It stands at zero or more remaining request segments and matches when every one of them is empty or decodes by HY-6. <a id="HY-49.3"></a> Its value is the rest of the request path without decoding: `/` followed by the remaining segments joined with `/`, or `/` when none remains.

## Data and topics

- **HY-10** <a id="HY-10.1"></a> Shared data is one map that the layout, the title and every region receive. <a id="HY-10.2"></a> It starts with `title`, the route title, and `csrf`, the masked session token of HY-24 for this response, then `context`, the context of the application (HY-124), when the application declares one, followed by the values that the application adds. <a id="HY-10.3"></a> When the read paths of the route (HY-73) remove `csrf`, `context` comes right after `title`, and when they remove both, it comes first; placing the context in shared data that already holds a member `context` fails, with HY-43 on a server and with an error in the browser, because the context has one place and one source.

- **HY-11** <a id="HY-11.1"></a> Every non-page region declares the topics it uses. <a id="HY-11.2"></a> A topic names data that can change, such as `posts`. <a id="HY-11.3"></a> The topic `path` is built in: it changes when the request path differs from the path of the `HX-Current-URL` request header after removing the base path. <a id="HY-11.4"></a> The current path is the path of the URL of `HX-Current-URL` with its bytes read as UTF-8, and it is absent when the request has no such header, when the URL has no path, and when the bytes are not valid UTF-8.

## Rendering

- **HY-12** <a id="HY-12.1"></a> A document is the layout rendered with root data equal to the shared data and with `html` definitions: `title` (the title rendered alone), `data` (HY-31), `build` (HY-125) and one per manifest region, the region rendered alone. <a id="HY-12.2"></a> The page region template is the route template.

- **HY-13** <a id="HY-13.1"></a> A region rendered alone uses the region template and the root data `merge(shared, region data)`, where a region data value replaces a shared value with the same name. <a id="HY-13.2"></a> The page region receives every route region of its route, rendered alone, as an `html` definition. <a id="HY-13.3"></a> The title rendered alone uses the title template and the shared data. <a id="HY-13.4"></a> The server and the browser compose documents and region parts in this same way, so they produce the same bytes. <a id="HY-13.5"></a> A document or a region response binds each of its roots once with the bound map of the template engine (VAL-22): the shared data, the data of every region and, in a document that embeds its data, the embedded data (HY-31). <a id="HY-13.6"></a> Every render of the response uses those bound maps and `merge`, so the number of binds does not grow with the number of renders; a shared value is bound in the shared data and once more in the embedded data of a document that embeds its data, because the embedded data carries the shared data. <a id="HY-13.7"></a> The PHP and Python servers read a shared value that a handler returns once for the check of HY-44, once in the bound shared data of a document, once more in the embedded data of a document that embeds its data, and once for the JSON text of a JSON response, so they read the value twice for a document, three times for a document that embeds its data and twice for a JSON response.

- **HY-14** <a id="HY-14.1"></a> Server and browser render with the same environment. <a id="HY-14.2"></a> The server sends the time zone in every JSON response.

- **HY-48** <a id="HY-48.1"></a> A server renders documents and regions as HY-12 and HY-13 define, with the template engine of its runtime, from the outputs of the build (HR-96): the manifest, the templates of the application, the read paths `reads.json` (HY-73) and the build id `build.json` (HY-125). <a id="HY-48.2"></a> It opens the application only when every output that it needs exists: `open` fails with the absolute path of the first missing output, so that a missing build fails when the application opens and names the missing file. <a id="HY-48.3"></a> The build first rejects `hx-*` attributes outside the layout (HC-6 of the [application authoring rules](../operations/composition.md)) and checks the templates with the rules of HY-3 (with the placement `{# build}`, HY-125), HY-30 and HY-75, the same rules as `hyper check` (HR-96), and a violation fails the build with every problem before it removes or writes any output, so a server program never serves templates that break them. <a id="HY-48.13"></a> One rule of the Rust core holds that check and gives every problem as a line that names the template, in this order: the `hx-*` attributes of each template other than the layout whose name ends with `.tpl`, in the byte order of the names and the order of their lines, then the placements of `{# title}`, `{# data}` and `{# build}`, of the manifest regions and of the page region in the layout, then the route regions of each route in manifest order. <a id="HY-48.12"></a> Node: `App.open` fails when the template index is not a template index or does not hold a template of a route.

  - <a id="HY-48.4"></a> PHP: PHP renders with a program that the build compiles from the application templates: with the generated PHP program of the same templates, through the API of the template package, which the native template extension `polyspec_template` registers under the same names when PHP has loaded it, so that the server holds no branch on the extension. <a id="HY-48.5"></a> The program passes the same tests and `make parity` with and without the extension. <a id="HY-48.6"></a> The build compiles the generated program into a PHP namespace that the application chooses and writes it into the directory `php` of the program directory as PSR-4 files, one class per file named after its class, so it declares no global name and the programs of several applications load in one PHP process. <a id="HY-48.7"></a> The application maps that namespace to that directory in `autoload.psr-4` of its `composer.json`, and the server takes the class `GeneratedProgram` of the namespace that `program.json` names through the autoload of Composer and requires no file of the program itself. <a id="HY-48.8"></a> `App::open` fails when the program directory has no directory `php`, no `program.json`, no `reads.json` (HY-73), no `build.json` (HY-125) or no directory `templates`, with the absolute path of the first missing one. <a id="HY-48.9"></a> It also fails when the autoload does not load that class, naming the class and the directory `php` that `autoload.psr-4` must map to its namespace.
  - <a id="HY-48.10"></a> Python: the program directory holds `reads.json`, `build.json` and the directory `templates`; `App.open` fails with a `ValueError` (HY-106) that names the first missing one. <a id="HY-48.14"></a> Python: until the Python server calls the core, the program directory also holds the file `legacy/hyper/data.tpl` (HY-31.10), which the loader of the server reads beside the directory `templates`, and `App.open` fails in the same way when it is missing.
  - <a id="HY-48.11"></a> Node: `App.open` reads the manifest, the template index, the template files and the build id file by absolute paths, the last from its option `build`, the absolute path of `client/build.json` of the build output (HY-125); a missing file fails with the error that names its path.

## Requests

- **HY-15** <a id="HY-15.1"></a> A request that selects `application/vnd.hyper+json` (HY-116) and has `HX-Request: true`, which htmx sends with every request, is a region request; one that selects it without `HX-Request` is a document request. <a id="HY-15.2"></a> A request that selects `text/html` is an HTML request and receives an HTML document. <a id="HY-15.3"></a> A JSON response has `Content-Type: application/vnd.hyper+json`. <a id="HY-15.4"></a> A region request always updates the page region (HY-18). <a id="HY-15.5"></a> `application/json` is not a media type of hyper, so an application can give it its own meaning in a representation (HY-118).

- **HY-56** <a id="HY-56.1"></a> The raw query of a request is the request target after its first `?` up to its first `#`, or empty text without a `?`. <a id="HY-56.9"></a> The query values are the values that `parse_urlencoded` of http-form reads from the raw query without nesting (F-20), a list of each name in the order of its first occurrence with its values in request order (F-20.3); a name or a value that is not UTF-8 fails with HY-42. <a id="HY-56.5"></a> `Request` provides the raw query and the query values, and `queryInt` reads the last value of a name. <a id="HY-56.7"></a> `query()`, `form()` and `files()` of a request return a list of pairs of a name and its values in the three servers, so that a decimal name stays a string. <a id="HY-56.8"></a> `queryInt(name, default)` returns the last value as an integer when it is an optional `-` and 1 to 15 decimal digits, and the default otherwise.

- **HY-57** <a id="HY-57.13"></a> The form values of a request are the form values of its body that F-21 of http-form reads without nesting: an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body is read by F-20, a `multipart/form-data` body gives its parts without a `filename`, and a body of another type or without `Content-Type` has none (F-21.4); a name or a value that is not UTF-8 fails with HY-42 (F-21.5). <a id="HY-57.6"></a> The PHP server reads the body from `php://input`, not from `$_POST`, which nests bracketed names; PHP gives it the body of a `multipart/form-data` request only when `enable_post_data_reading` is off. <a id="HY-57.7"></a> `Request` provides the form values, and `formString` reads the last value of a name. <a id="HY-57.14"></a> The type of a body is read from its `Content-Type` by F-12 of http-form, and a parameter that its type does not define changes nothing (F-12.4): a `charset` or another parameter of an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body fails nothing, and the body is read as UTF-8.

- **HY-113** <a id="HY-113.21"></a> The files of a `multipart/form-data` body are the files of F-22 of http-form: a file is a part with a `name` and a `filename` parameter, also with an empty filename, and has its name, its filename as sent, its content type and its bytes (F-22.2), and `filename*` is not read (F-22.5). <a id="HY-113.22"></a> The header lines and the parameters of a part are read as F-23, F-6 and F-16 of http-form state, and its boundary as F-12.3 and F-7 state; a part that fails with kind `invalid`, `header_limit` or `no_boundary` of http-form fails the whole body (F-23.3) with status 400 as HY-42 does. <a id="HY-113.2"></a> The request gives its files as `files()`, a list of pairs of a name and its files in request order (HY-56.7), as HY-57 orders the form values, and `file(name)` returns the last file of a name, or null (`None` in Python) when it has none, as `formString` reads the last value. <a id="HY-113.8"></a> The file API is part of the public API of HY-106, in each runtime form: PHP `Request::files()` and `Request::file()`, Python `files()` and `file()`, and Node `files()` and `file()`, each with the class `UploadedFile`, whose methods `name()`, `filename()`, `contentType()` (`content_type()` in Python) and `content()` return the four parts of HY-113.21.

- **HY-114** <a id="HY-114.1"></a> The application may declare a file limit, the largest number of bytes of one file (HY-113), as an option of the application next to the body limit (HY-59). <a id="HY-114.2"></a> The default is 8 MiB, the same as the default body limit. <a id="HY-114.3"></a> An application that declares no file limit uses the smaller of 8 MiB and its body limit as its file limit, so that it opens with any body limit and refuses a file only when the body limit already refuses its request. <a id="HY-114.4"></a> The check of a declared file limit below applies only to a declared value. <a id="HY-114.11"></a> The file limit is the file limit of F-25.4 of http-form: it bounds the temporary storage of one file, and a file is never truncated and never passed in part. <a id="HY-114.6"></a> A file limit that is not a positive integer, or that is larger than the body limit, fails when the application opens, as HY-59 states for another limit. <a id="HY-114.7"></a> The server checks the bytes of each file part while it reads the body (HY-131.11): a file whose bytes are more than the file limit makes the request fail with status 413 and the text `Content Too Large`, as HY-59.4 does and at its place in the order of HY-59.3, and no action runs. <a id="HY-114.12"></a> `fileOver(limit)` of the request is `file_over` of F-27 of http-form on the files of its body, and a `limit` that is no unsigned integer fails with kind `invalid_number` of the binding before the files are compared.

- **HY-131** <a id="HY-131.26"></a> The server reads a `multipart/form-data` body in chunks as it arrives, for an application whose form types include `multipart/form-data` (HY-59.1), by the reader of F-24 of http-form, which holds neither the body nor the content of a file part as one value (F-24.1); its delimiters and the failures of its bytes are those of F-24.2 to F-24.5, the result does not depend on the chunks (F-24.6), and the first failure of a body is the failure whose byte comes first (F-8), so a body whose invalid byte comes before the body limit receives 400 as HY-42 does, not 413. <a id="HY-131.27"></a> The application may declare a value limit, the value limit of F-25.2 of http-form, which also bounds a body that an application or a test builds from bytes. <a id="HY-131.8"></a> An application that declares no value limit uses the smaller of 8 MiB and its body limit. <a id="HY-131.9"></a> The application may declare a part limit, the largest number of parts of a body, 1000 by default. <a id="HY-131.10"></a> A value limit or a part limit that is not a positive integer, or a value limit larger than the body limit, fails when the application opens, as HY-59.2 states. <a id="HY-131.11"></a> A body that passes the body limit, the value limit, the part limit or the file limit (HY-114) receives status 413 with the text `Content Too Large`, and every server stops reading the body when it passes a limit. <a id="HY-131.28"></a> The server writes the content of a file part, as it arrives, to the directory of the request of F-10 of http-form, and `UploadedFile` gives the bytes of its file as `size()`, moves it with `moveTo(path)` (`move_to` in Python) and reads it with `content()` as F-11 states, so that a path that exists and a file that was moved fail with the kinds `exists` and `moved` of http-form. <a id="HY-131.14"></a> It removes the directory after the response hook (HY-60) or the disconnect hook (HY-67) of the request returned, also for a request that fails; a file that the application moved is not in it. <a id="HY-131.18"></a> The checks keep the order of HY-59.3: a `Content-Length` larger than the body limit receives 413 before the body is read; the limits of this rule and the failures of HY-42 answer while the body is read; then routing, the form type (HY-59.12) and the CSRF token (HY-59.8) answer, and a request that they refuse leaves no temporary file. <a id="HY-131.29"></a> A `Content-Length` that is no number receives status 400 with kind `invalid_content_length` of http-form before the body is read (F-9), and the host passes the field value to the core, which compares it with the body limit (F-25.1). <a id="HY-131.19"></a> A request with a slow client or without an end is the task of the server in front of the application, which this rule gives no time limit. <a id="HY-131.25"></a> The Node host reads a body in paused mode: on each `'readable'` event it takes the bytes that `request.read()` gives as one buffer, awaits `feed` of that buffer and reads again only after it settled, and it joins no chunks, because joining would pass the bound of HY-131.26 and delay the check of a limit; the PHP and Python servers feed a chunk before they read the next one.

## Media types and representations

A route has one resource and one or more representations of it (RFC 9110, section 3.2): its page as `text/html`, its page data as `application/vnd.hyper+json`, and the media types that it declares. hyper selects the representation, checks the request and writes the response of every one of them, so that an application serves a JSON contract for other clients through the same router, the same limits and the same response rules as its pages.

- **HY-116** <a id="HY-116.1"></a> The server selects the media type of every request, except `<base path>/_hyper/keep` (HY-40), among `text/html`, `application/vnd.hyper+json` and the representation types of its route (HY-118), after the selection of HY-62, the removal of the data base path of a chosen request (HY-62.19) and the routing of the path (HY-27, 404), because the types depend on the route. <a id="HY-116.2"></a> It selects once, and the request holds the selected type and, for a representation, its parameter values; the request kinds of HY-15, the request methods that report them, and every later step read them from the request and do not read `Accept` again. <a id="HY-116.17"></a> The server reads the `Accept` field lines of a request, as its host gives them, with `Accept.parse` of http-negotiation (NG-5, NG-6): a request without `Accept` states no preference (NG-5.1), each field line is a list read on its own (NG-5.2), and a field whose lines hold no range is the empty list, which matches no type (NG-5.3). <a id="HY-116.18"></a> A field that NG-5.7 refuses, with kind `invalid_accept` or `invalid_weight`, receives status 400 with the text `Bad Request`: such as a range `*/html`, a parameter given twice (NG-3.5), a quoted string without its end, a weight that is not a qvalue (NG-6.1) and anything after the weight, an accept extension included, which RFC 9110 no longer defines (appendix B.3). <a id="HY-116.19"></a> The server weighs its types with `Accept.weigh` of http-negotiation (NG-7 to NG-10): `text/html` and `application/vnd.hyper+json` are candidates with `matching` `ignore` and `wildcards` true, because they have no parameters, and each declared type of the route (HY-118) is a candidate with `matching` `exact`, `wildcards` false and the served values of its required parameters, so that `type/*`, `*/*` and a range without a served value of every required parameter give it no weight. <a id="HY-116.20"></a> A weight of 0 makes a type not acceptable (NG-6.3), and a value of a range equals a served value as NG-8.4 compares them: quoting does not matter and the values of `charset` compare without case. <a id="HY-116.11"></a> The server takes the type of the highest weight, and among equal weights the first in the order `text/html`, `application/vnd.hyper+json`, then the declared order. <a id="HY-116.12"></a> It then checks the method against the selected type: `methods` for a representation (HY-121), HY-27 for a page. <a id="HY-116.13"></a> A request that matches none of the types receives status 406 with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `Vary: Accept` and a body that lists the types that its path serves, each on a line that ends with a line feed, in the order `text/html`, `application/vnd.hyper+json` and the declared order; a declared type is listed once for each combination of one served value of every required parameter, in the order in which `parameters` lists the served values of the first parameter, then of the next, which is the declared order and no sorted order, and written as the `Content-Type` of HY-119. <a id="HY-116.14"></a> Under a chosen request of HY-62, the path of HY-62.19 serves no `text/html` and the path of HY-62.22 serves only `text/html`. <a id="HY-116.15"></a> A representation is answered only under the data base path (HY-62.19); a request of HY-62.22 receives the 404 and the 405 of HY-62.23 before the selection, so a request of HY-62.22 with a method other than `GET` or `HEAD` receives 405 also when no type of the route is acceptable. <a id="HY-116.21"></a> A request holds the selected media type only after the selection, and asking a request without it whether it wants JSON or is a region request fails with kind `not_selected`, of the category `type`, because it is an error of the order of the calls.

- **HY-117** <a id="HY-117.1"></a> A response with `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json` has `Vary: Accept, HX-Request, HX-Current-URL`, followed by `, Hyper-Context` when the application declares a context (HY-124); the shell of HY-62 has the same `Vary`. <a id="HY-117.2"></a> Every response that a representation request receives after the selection, which are the 405, 415 and 400 of HY-121, the response of its handler and its 304 (HY-122) and the 404 and 412 of HY-107, has `Vary: Accept` followed by the `vary` names of its entry (HY-118). <a id="HY-117.3"></a> The 400 and the 406 of HY-116 and the 406 of HY-62.20 and HY-62.34 have `Vary: Accept`, because `Accept` decides them. <a id="HY-117.4"></a> Every other plain text response, the 500 of HY-43 and HY-66 of a representation request included, has no `Vary`, because it has `Cache-Control: no-store` (HY-65) and `Accept` does not decide it. <a id="HY-117.5"></a> A cache gives a stored response only to a request whose listed headers are equal (RFC 9110, section 12.5.5; RFC 9111, section 4.1), so a response never reaches a request that would have received another.

- **HY-118** <a id="HY-118.1"></a> A route may declare `representations`, an ordered list. <a id="HY-118.2"></a> Each entry has `type`, a media type; `parameters`, a map from each required parameter name of the type to the list of the values that the entry serves, such as `{"version": ["1"]}`, or an empty map; `methods`, a nonempty subset of `GET`, `POST`, `PUT` and `DELETE`; and `vary`, the request header names that its responses depend on besides `Accept`, such as `Authorization`, or an empty list. <a id="HY-118.3"></a> An entry with `GET` also answers `HEAD` with the headers of its `GET` response and no body (RFC 9110, section 9.3.2). <a id="HY-118.4"></a> The application provides one representation handler for each entry, by the route name and the type. <a id="HY-118.5"></a> The manifest check (HY-2) rejects, comparing without regard to case, a duplicate type in one route, a type equal to `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json`, a type whose type or subtype is `*`, a parameter named `q`, a type, a parameter name or a value that is not valid (RFC 9110, section 8.3.1), an empty `methods`, an empty value list, a `vary` name that is not a field name (RFC 9110, section 5.1), a `vary` name `Accept` or `Cookie` and two equal `vary` names; opening the application fails for an entry without a handler and for a handler of a type that its route does not declare. <a id="HY-118.6"></a> A served value holds only HTAB, SP and the characters U+0021 to U+007E, and the manifest check rejects a value with another character, because a header carries a character above U+007E in bytes that differ between UTF-8 and ISO-8859-1. <a id="HY-118.7"></a> `parameters` is a JSON object, and `methods`, `vary` and each value list are JSON arrays; the manifest check rejects another JSON value in their place, also an empty array in place of the empty object.

- **HY-119** <a id="HY-119.5"></a> The handler of a declared type receives the parameter values of the range that decides its weight (NG-10.3). <a id="HY-119.4"></a> The `Content-Type` of the response is the media type that `format` of http-media-type writes (MT-6) from the type and, for each required parameter in the order of `parameters`, its name and the selected value, so a name is in lower case and a value is quoted only when it is not a token.

- **HY-120** <a id="HY-120.1"></a> The application opens the session of a request with the session store that its host passes to it (HY-97, HY-100), only for `<base path>/_hyper/keep` (HY-40) and for a request that selects `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json` (HY-116). <a id="HY-120.2"></a> It opens it after the checks of HY-116, HY-62 (its 405, 406 and shell), HY-127, HY-59.12 and HY-114 that apply to the request, and before the token check of HY-24 and the first handler, because the token check is the first step that reads the session. <a id="HY-120.3"></a> A request that one of those checks refuses opens no session and waits for no lock of HY-104. <a id="HY-120.4"></a> A representation request therefore opens no session, holds no lock of HY-104 and sets no session cookie. <a id="HY-120.6"></a> The opening of the session of a page request reads and removes the flash data and then reads the token, which it sets when the session holds none. <a id="HY-120.7"></a> The opening of the session of a request to `<base path>/_hyper/keep` reads only the token, which it sets when the session holds none, and leaves the flash data in the session, because the kept endpoint answers no page and the flash data belongs to the next page request (HY-25.2).

- **HY-121** <a id="HY-121.1"></a> A representation request runs its handler and no context handler, loader, action or shared handler; the handler reads the selection value of HY-62 from its request, as a loader does. <a id="HY-121.2"></a> The server reads no session and no cookie, sets no cookie and sends no `csrf`, and the request that the handler receives has no `Cookie` header, so the response depends only on the request line, the headers other than `Cookie`, the body and the stored data that the handler reads. <a id="HY-121.3"></a> A request that writes with a session is an action (HY-24). <a id="HY-121.4"></a> The method check of HY-116 comes before the 415 and the 400 of this rule. <a id="HY-121.5"></a> A `HEAD` request of an entry with `GET` runs the handler with the request method `GET`; `App.handle` returns that `GET` response with its body, which the response hook (HY-60), the response limit (HY-66) and `around` (HY-97) receive, and the host writes its status and its headers, with the `Content-Length` of that body, and no body. <a id="HY-121.6"></a> A method that `methods` does not list, other than `HEAD` for an entry with `GET`, receives 405 with `Allow`, which lists the methods that the entry answers in the order `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, separated by `, `. <a id="HY-121.7"></a> A `GET`, `HEAD` or `DELETE` whose body has a size (HY-59.5) other than 0 receives 400 with the text `Bad Request`, because these methods carry no body that the handler reads. <a id="HY-121.11"></a> A `POST` or `PUT` without `Content-Type`, or whose media type (MT-4) is not `application/json`, receives 415, and one whose `Content-Type` is no media type receives 400 with the text `Bad Request` (HY-59.12); the body limit of HY-59 applies, and a body that is not valid UTF-8, that json refuses or whose value is outside the data model, as HY-54.20 reads it, receives 400 with the text `Bad Request`. <a id="HY-121.9"></a> The handler reads the decoded value with `json()` of its request (PHP `Request::json()`, Node and Python `request.json()`). <a id="HY-121.10"></a> The request that the handler receives holds the route parameters of its path (HY-5).

- **HY-122** <a id="HY-122.1"></a> A representation handler returns a response with a status, a body, and headers; the body is a value of the data model other than null, or null, which means that the response has no body. <a id="HY-122.2"></a> The status is one of 200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 406, 409, 412, 415, 422 and 428; a 401 requires `WWW-Authenticate`, a 201 requires `Location`, and a 204 with a body and a 200 without a body fail with HY-43. <a id="HY-122.3"></a> A response without a body has no `Content-Type`. <a id="HY-122.4"></a> The handler may set only `Location`, `WWW-Authenticate` and `Cache-Control` (HY-130). <a id="HY-122.5"></a> A `Location` that is an application path (HY-46) gets the base path of the request, the data base path under a chosen request (HY-62.19), as every `Location` of the application does (HY-8); a `Location` that is an absolute URI (RFC 3986, section 4.3) is sent as it is; another value, such as `//host/path` or `posts/8`, fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-122.6"></a> A response without a `Cache-Control` from the handler has `Cache-Control: no-cache`, or `private, no-cache` for a request with `Authorization`; for such a request, a handler value without the directive `private` or `no-store`, or with `public` or `s-maxage`, fails with HY-43, as HY-52 requires of a page (RFC 9111, section 3.5); directive names compare without regard to case (RFC 9111, section 5.2). <a id="HY-122.7"></a> A response with a status of 400 or more has `Cache-Control: no-store` (HY-65), and a handler that sets `Cache-Control` on it fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-122.8"></a> Another header or status fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-122.9"></a> The server writes the body as the JSON text of HY-54 with the `Content-Type` of HY-119. <a id="HY-122.10"></a> A response with status 200 to a `GET` or `HEAD` has the strong `ETag` `"<digits>"` of the first 32 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 digest of the `Content-Type`, a line feed and the body; a `GET` or `HEAD` whose `If-None-Match` equals it receives 304 with the headers of the 200 response except `Content-Type` and no body, as HY-53 states, and the tag is strong, unlike that of HY-53, because no token varies its bytes; a response with another status has no `ETag`, and an `If-None-Match` does not change it. <a id="HY-122.11"></a> The server gives the handler the function `etag(body)`, which returns that tag for a body of the selected type, so that a `PUT` or `DELETE` handler compares `If-Match` with it (RFC 9110, section 13.1.1). <a id="HY-122.12"></a> The response hook (HY-60, with a new empty reply), the frame policy (HY-45), the response limit (HY-66), the errors of the ORM (HY-107: `no_rows` is 404 with the text `Not Found`, and `revision_changed` is 412 with the text `Precondition Failed`, both plain text with `Cache-Control: no-store`) and the errors of HY-43 apply as to a page; HY-52, HY-53 for its weak tag and HY-103 do not, because the handler has no reply. <a id="HY-122.13"></a> `etag(body)` fails with the error of the data model (HY-44) for a body that is not a value of the data model.

## JSON response

- **HY-17** <a id="HY-17.1"></a> A JSON response has this shape. <a id="HY-17.2"></a> Keys keep their order. <a id="HY-17.3"></a> Every server writes the JSON text of a response, and decodes the kept values of HY-38 and HY-40, as HY-54 states.

```json
{
  "env": { "timezone": "+09:00" },
  "route": "board.show",
  "params": { "id": "7" },
  "build": "<build id>",
  "context": { "hash": "<context hash>", "value": { "name": "Board" } },
  "shared": { "title": "Post", "csrf": "token" },
  "regions": {
    "content": { "post": { "id": 7 } },
    "reader": { "large": false },
    "left": { "count": 3 }
  },
  "kept": {
    "reader": { "large": true }
  }
}
```

`build` is the build id (HY-125); `context` is present only for an application with a context and holds `value` only as HY-128 states. `regions` holds the loader data. `kept` holds, by region and path, the `server` and `cookie` kept values that the server read for the regions in `regions` and that conform to the region data (HY-38). A region without such values has no entry.

- **HY-18** <a id="HY-18.1"></a> For a document request, `regions` contains every region in manifest order, without absent route regions (HY-75). <a id="HY-18.2"></a> For a region request, it contains the page region first, then every other region that uses a changed topic, in manifest order. <a id="HY-18.3"></a> The page region of a route without a loader has the empty map as its data.

- **HY-19** <a id="HY-19.1"></a> The changed topics of a request are the topics recorded by the previous action (HY-25) and `path` (HY-11).

## Application context

An application sends with every JSON response values that change only with its configuration and its build, such as messages, asset URLs and names. The context holds them: a part of the shared data that the browser holds by its hash, and that a JSON response holds only when it changed.

- **HY-124** <a id="HY-124.1"></a> An application may declare a context handler. <a id="HY-124.2"></a> The server calls it once for every request that selects `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json` (HY-116) and that reaches the shared handler, which is a request without an action, a request whose action returns the route page (HY-26, HY-58) and a request whose action lets `REVISION_CHANGED` escape, which the server answers as the page with status 409 (HY-107), after the action of the request and before the shared handler and any loader, so that the context holds what the action wrote, with the value of the selection of HY-62 (null for an application without client rendering), and the handler returns a map of the data model (HY-44), the context. <a id="HY-124.3"></a> A loader or the shared handler that then stops or fails the request does not undo the call. <a id="HY-124.4"></a> A request whose action redirects (HY-25, HY-50), stops (HY-51, HY-58) or fails with HY-43, and a request that hyper answers before any handler runs, cause no call. <a id="HY-124.5"></a> The handler reads no value of the request: no path, no parameter, no query, no header, no session and no cookie. <a id="HY-124.6"></a> The context therefore depends only on the selection value, the build and the stored data that the handler reads, and its hash (HY-125) identifies it. <a id="HY-124.7"></a> The context is the member `context` of the shared data (HY-10); templates read it as `context.<name>`. <a id="HY-124.8"></a> A shared handler that returns the key `context` fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-124.9"></a> An application without the declaration has no member `context`. <a id="HY-124.10"></a> In Node the context is a `Map` (HY-54), because a plain object orders its integer-like keys first and would give another JSON text than PHP and Python; a Node context handler may return a promise of it, which the server awaits, and another value fails with HY-43.

- **HY-125** <a id="HY-125.15"></a> The build id is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of every file that one build writes and that does not hold the id: the files below `public/assets` of the application that `client/assets.json` lists, the files below `client/` and below `program/` of `--output`, and the bytes of every `--static` file, which the static shell of HY-62 serves. <a id="HY-125.16"></a> It leaves out `client/build.json` and `program/build.json`, the static shell `csr/index.html`, which holds the id, and the copies below `csr/assets`, which hold the bytes of the files below `public/assets`. <a id="HY-125.17"></a> The path of a file is its path with the prefix of its place: `public/assets/<name>` for a file below `public/assets`, `client/<path>` and `program/<path>` for a file below those directories of `--output`, and `csr/<path>` for a `--static` file and the other files of the static shell; a path with another prefix, with nothing after its prefix, or with a segment that is empty, `.` or `..`, and a path given twice, fail the build with the kind `invalid_build` and the path. <a id="HY-125.3"></a> The build hashes the outputs in the order of their paths, compared as bytes, each path as UTF-8 followed by a NUL byte, the length of its file as 8 bytes big-endian and the bytes of the file. <a id="HY-125.18"></a> It writes the id as `{"build":"<build id>"}` into `build.json` of `program/` and of `client/`, and every server reads the id when the application opens; `open` fails with the absolute path of a `build.json` that is missing or that does not hold exactly the key `build` with a build id. <a id="HY-125.19"></a> A build id is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; one rule of the core checks that form with the kind `invalid_build`, for the open of every server and for the build. <a id="HY-125.20"></a> So a build id names one build output: a build that changes only a server output gives a new id, an open page reads the page again at its next navigation (HYC-22), and every server of one deployment, also servers of several runtimes that share sessions, reads one build output. <a id="HY-125.21"></a> The build takes no build id from its caller: one run of `hyper build` computes the id once from the outputs that it writes and has no option that sets the id or names a file that holds it, so no build output is changed after its build. <a id="HY-125.7"></a> A document has the `html` definition `build`, the text `<meta name="hyper-build" content="<build id>">`, which the layout renders with `{# build}` once inside `<head>` (HY-3, HY-12); the build fails for a layout that does not place `{# build}` exactly once, as for `{# title}` and `{# data}` (HY-48); the check counts the placement and does not check that it lies inside `<head>`. <a id="HY-125.8"></a> The static shell has the same element. <a id="HY-125.14"></a> The name `hyper-build` is the name of the build id element of a hyper application and has nothing to do with the names of the packages (HR-98), so it stays when a package is renamed. <a id="HY-125.9"></a> The server checks the context by HY-44 for every request that calls the context handler. <a id="HY-125.10"></a> For a JSON response and for a document that embeds its data (HY-31), and for no other response, it then writes the JSON text of HY-54 of the context once and computes the context hash from it; that text is the text of the member `value` of HY-128 and the text of the hash below. <a id="HY-125.11"></a> A document that does not embed its data holds neither the hash nor `value`, so the server renders it from the context map and does not write that text. <a id="HY-125.12"></a> The context hash is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of the bytes `{"build":"<build id>","context":`, then that text, then `}`, which is the JSON text of HY-54 of that map, so every server computes the same hash for the same context, and a new build gives a new hash.

- **HY-126** <a id="HY-126.1"></a> The read paths of HY-73 do not apply to `context`: the server sends it whole, because one context serves every route and its hash covers all of it. <a id="HY-126.2"></a> HY-71 applies to it as to all shared data.

- **HY-127** <a id="HY-127.1"></a> A region request and a document request may send the header `Hyper-Context` with the context hash that the browser holds. <a id="HY-127.2"></a> An application with a context checks the header of every request that selects `text/html` or `application/vnd.hyper+json` and that HY-62 does not answer with its 405, 406 or shell, right after the method check of HY-116 and before HY-59.12 and HY-59.8, the file limit of HY-114, the token check of HY-24, the context handler and any loader or action: a value that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters makes the server respond with status 400 and the text `Bad Request` (HY-58). <a id="HY-127.3"></a> An application without a context does not read the header. <a id="HY-127.4"></a> An HTML request with a valid value is answered as without it, because a document holds the whole context.

- **HY-128** <a id="HY-128.1"></a> Every JSON response (HY-17) holds, after `params`, the member `build`, the build id. <a id="HY-128.2"></a> A JSON response of an application with a context holds after it the member `context`: `{"hash": <context hash>}`, followed by `"value": <context>` when the request has no `Hyper-Context` or names another hash. <a id="HY-128.3"></a> The member `context` of `shared` is absent from a JSON response; before it renders, the browser code inserts the context into `shared` at its position of HY-10: the `value` of the response when it has one, and otherwise the held context. <a id="HY-128.4"></a> The Node server renders its documents with that same code (HY-54) from the context map, and puts the member `context` with `hash` and `value` into the value that it renders only for a document that embeds its data. <a id="HY-128.5"></a> A document that embeds its data (HY-31) embeds `build` and `context` with `value`.

## Browser

- **HYC-1** <a id="HYC-1.1"></a> The browser code routes the response URL path (after removing the base path) with the manifest routes. <a id="HYC-1.2"></a> The route name must equal `route` in the response; otherwise rendering fails. <a id="HYC-1.3"></a> The page region template is the template of that route. <a id="HYC-1.4"></a> The browser code routes a request path by HY-4 to HY-8 and HY-49.

- **HYC-2** <a id="HYC-2.1"></a> The htmx extension requests JSON (`Accept: application/vnd.hyper+json`) only when the `id` of the request target element is the name of the page region. <a id="HYC-2.2"></a> It converts a JSON region response into this HTML and gives it to htmx in place of the response text: `<title>` with the title rendered alone, then the page region rendered alone, then `<hx-partial hx-target="#<name>" hx-swap="innerMorph">` with each other region rendered alone. <a id="HYC-2.3"></a> Before htmx swaps, the browser applies the stylesheet links of the layout of the response (HYC-15) and creates its module scripts (HYC-25). <a id="HYC-2.4"></a> htmx then performs the swap, the title change and the history update. <a id="HYC-2.5"></a> A response whose content type is not `application/vnd.hyper+json` passes unchanged.

- **HYC-8** <a id="HYC-8.1"></a> In client-side rendering, a static shell declares the base path of the server with `<meta name="hyper-api" content="/api">`. <a id="HYC-8.2"></a> The browser code requests the document JSON for the current path while it loads the templates of the route (HYC-12), routes the response URL after redirects (HYC-1), renders the document (HY-12), applies the stylesheet links of its head (HYC-15), creates its module scripts (HYC-25), replaces the attributes of the `html` element (HYC-6), the title and the body with the rendered ones, and lets htmx process the new body. <a id="HYC-8.3"></a> A current path that matches no route renders the body text `Not Found`.

- **HYC-3** <a id="HYC-3.1"></a> In client-side rendering, the extension prefixes the same-origin request path of every region request with the base path, removes the base path from history paths, and replaces htmx history restoration with HYC-8 for the restored path. <a id="HYC-3.2"></a> A later restoration cancels an earlier one that is still loading, and only the latest one is rendered; HYC-23 orders restorations with region requests.

- **HYC-15** <a id="HYC-15.1"></a> The stylesheet links of a head are its `link` elements that have an `href` attribute and whose `rel` attribute contains the token `stylesheet`, compared without regard to ASCII case. <a id="HYC-15.2"></a> The key of a link is the value of its `href` attribute resolved against the URL of the page. <a id="HYC-15.3"></a> When the browser shows new content, it applies the stylesheet links of the head of a source document to the head of the page:

  - <a id="HYC-15.4"></a> client-side rendering of a document (HYC-8, HYC-3): the rendered document;
  - <a id="HYC-15.5"></a> a JSON region response (HYC-2): the layout rendered with the shared data of the response, with the context of HY-128 as its member `context`, as root data, the title rendered alone as the definition `title`, the definition `build` of the build of the page (HYC-22), and an empty definition `data` and an empty definition for every manifest region;
  - <a id="HYC-15.6"></a> the HTML document that htmx requests to restore a page from history in server-side rendering (HYC-4): that document.

  <a id="HYC-15.7"></a> The browser applies the links in three steps:

  1. <a id="HYC-15.8"></a> It walks the stylesheet links of the source in order; a key that appears again counts only at its first link. <a id="HYC-15.9"></a> For each link it keeps the first stylesheet link of the page with the same key that stands after the last kept link, and otherwise inserts a copy of the source link after the last kept or inserted link, or, before the first kept link, in front of the first stylesheet link of the page, or at the end of the head when the page has none.
  2. <a id="HYC-15.10"></a> It waits until every inserted link, and every kept link that an earlier application inserted and that is still loading, has loaded. <a id="HYC-15.11"></a> Only then does it show the content.
  3. <a id="HYC-15.12"></a> After it shows the content, it removes every other stylesheet link of the page, so that the stylesheet links of the page are those of the source in their order.

  <a id="HYC-15.13"></a> Other elements of the head, such as `style` elements, stay. <a id="HYC-15.14"></a> When a later application starts before an earlier one shows its content, only the later one removes links. <a id="HYC-15.15"></a> When a link, or a module script of the same application (HYC-25), fails to load, the browser removes the links that it inserted for this application, does not show the content and reports the failure as HYC-14 defines. <a id="HYC-15.16"></a> The first document of server-side rendering already has its stylesheet links and needs no application.

- **HYC-25** <a id="HYC-25.1"></a> The module scripts of a head are its `script` elements that have a `src` attribute and whose `type` attribute, without leading and trailing ASCII whitespace, is `module`, compared without regard to ASCII case. <a id="HYC-25.2"></a> The key of a script is the value of its `src` attribute resolved against the URL of the page. <a id="HYC-25.3"></a> When the browser applies the stylesheet links of a source document (HYC-15), it also creates the module scripts of the head of that document in the page, as part of the same application. <a id="HYC-25.4"></a> The page holds the key of each `script` element of its document, in the head or the body, that has a `src` attribute and the type `module` as defined above, and the key of the `content` of its `<meta name="hyper-entry">`, the client entry that a static shell inlines (HYC-16). <a id="HYC-25.5"></a> In a page with `<meta name="hyper-api">` and without `<meta name="hyper-entry">`, such as a shell that `hyper build` did not write, the browser cannot tell the entry from another module script, so an application that would create a script fails before it creates one, as a script that does not load (HYC-14). <a id="HYC-25.6"></a> The browser walks the module scripts of the source in order; a key that appears again counts only at its first script. <a id="HYC-25.7"></a> For each key that the page does not hold, it creates a `script` element of the page with the attributes of the source script and puts it at the end of the head of the page. <a id="HYC-25.8"></a> It sets the `async` property of a created script to whether the source script has the attribute `async`, so that the created scripts of one application run in the order of the source, as the module scripts of a parsed head do. <a id="HYC-25.9"></a> It shows the content only after every created script, and every module script of the page with a key of the source that an earlier application created and that is still loading, has loaded, so a module script runs before the new content is in the page. <a id="HYC-25.10"></a> It removes no script when it shows content, so a script of the page stays when a later source does not name it. <a id="HYC-25.11"></a> When a script or a stylesheet link of the application fails to load, the browser removes the scripts that it created for this application, does not show the content and reports the failure as HYC-14 defines. <a id="HYC-25.12"></a> The browser creates no other `script` element of a source head, such as a script without `src` or a script of another type. <a id="HYC-25.13"></a> The first document of server-side rendering already runs its module scripts and needs no application.

- **HYC-22** <a id="HYC-22.1"></a> The build of the page is the `hyper-build` of its document (HY-125), and the browser renders the definition `build` with it. <a id="HYC-22.2"></a> The browser holds the context and its hash: from the embedded data, or from the first JSON response, whose request has no `Hyper-Context`. <a id="HYC-22.3"></a> A document without `#hy-data` holds no context, so its next JSON request has no `Hyper-Context`. <a id="HYC-22.4"></a> The browser sends the held hash with every region request and document request (HY-127). <a id="HYC-22.5"></a> A response with `value` replaces the held context before the browser renders. <a id="HYC-22.9"></a> A response whose `build` differs from the build of the page makes the browser load the page URL of the response (HYC-1, without the data base path of HY-62) as a new document with `GET` instead of rendering, because the page holds the outputs of another build (HY-125.20). <a id="HYC-22.7"></a> When htmx restores a page from history by requesting its HTML (HYC-4), a document whose `hyper-build` differs from the build of the page is loaded as a new document instead of being swapped. <a id="HYC-22.8"></a> A response without `value` whose `hash` differs from the held hash is an error of the request (HYC-14).

- **HYC-23** <a id="HYC-23.1"></a> The browser renders only the response of its latest region request; the response of an earlier one is not rendered, as a later restoration cancels an earlier one (HYC-3). <a id="HYC-23.2"></a> A restoration (HYC-3, HYC-8) counts as a region request for this rule; a document request of HYC-7 does not, because HYC-7 drops its own response when another response replaced the held data. <a id="HYC-23.3"></a> A response that is not rendered is not a failure (HYC-14).

- **HYC-24** <a id="HYC-24.1"></a> `HyperOptions` of the browser code takes `functions`, a map from names to functions, and registers them in the template engine (template FUN-43). <a id="HYC-24.2"></a> The `App` of every server takes the same map as its option `functions` (HY-106) when the application opens, and the Node server registers it through `createApplication` of the browser code, so the server and the browser register the same names (template FUN-47); a registration that fails (template FUN-44) fails the open. <a id="HYC-24.5"></a> An entry that is not a function fails the open with the argument error of template RT-5. <a id="HYC-24.6"></a> A render that calls a name that is neither built in nor registered fails with HY-43.

## Client rendering on the server

- **HY-62** <a id="HY-62.1"></a> An application may declare client rendering, so that one server answers the client-rendered pages and the server-rendered pages of one manifest with the same handlers. <a id="HY-62.2"></a> The declaration has a static shell, a data base path and a selection:

  - <a id="HY-62.3"></a> The shell is the absolute path of an HTML file that contains `<meta name="hyper-api" content="<data base path>">` (HYC-8). <a id="HY-62.4"></a> The server reads it when the application opens.
  - <a id="HY-62.5"></a> The data base path follows HY-8 and is not empty. <a id="HY-62.6"></a> No route path is the data base path or starts with it followed by `/`.
  - <a id="HY-62.7"></a> The selection receives every request and returns a choice: whether the request is of a client-rendered page, chosen for example by the `Host` header, and a value, such as the stored service of the host. <a id="HY-62.8"></a> In PHP the choice is `new Choice(chosen: <bool>, value: <value>)`, and in Node it is `new Choice(chosen, value)` whose `chosen` is `true` or `false` and whose `value` is not `undefined`; a selection that returns another value fails as HY-62.11 states. <a id="HY-62.9"></a> The server calls the selection once per request, after HY-59.4 and HY-42 and before routing, with the request without its `Cookie` header: the choice decides the shell response and the path of a representation, and neither varies by `Cookie` (HY-117). <a id="HY-62.10"></a> In the Node server the selection may also return a promise of the choice, which the server awaits, because a selection that reads stored data reads it asynchronously in Node. <a id="HY-62.11"></a> A selection that throws, returns another value or returns a promise that rejects or resolves to another value fails with HY-43.
  - <a id="HY-62.12"></a> Every loader and action of the request reads the value of the choice from its request, `$request->selection()` in PHP and `request.selection()` in Node and Python, whether the selection chose the request or not. <a id="HY-62.13"></a> An application therefore reads the stored data that its selection and its handlers both need once per request and passes it as a value, without a cache. <a id="HY-62.14"></a> A request of an application without the declaration has the value null.

  <a id="HY-62.15"></a> The application fails to open when the shell file cannot be read, the shell does not declare the data base path, the data base path is empty or does not follow HY-8, or a route path lies under the data base path. <a id="HY-62.16"></a> A request that the selection does not choose is answered as without the declaration, with the base path of the application (HY-8). <a id="HY-62.17"></a> A chosen request is answered with the data base path in place of the base path of the application:

  1. <a id="HY-62.18"></a> `<data base path>/_hyper/keep` follows HY-40.
  2. <a id="HY-62.19"></a> A request path that starts with the data base path followed by `/` or the end of the path is routed after the data base path is removed, and `Location` headers include the data base path (HY-8). <a id="HY-62.20"></a> After the selection and the method check of HY-116, a request that selects a representation is answered by HY-121, and a request that selects `text/html` receives status 406 with the text `Not Acceptable` and `Vary: Accept`. <a id="HY-62.21"></a> Every other request is answered by HY-15 to HY-40 and HY-42 to HY-59: a document request and a region request receive JSON, and an action runs.
  3. <a id="HY-62.22"></a> Any other request path is routed as it is. <a id="HY-62.23"></a> A path without a route receives 404 and a method other than `GET` or `HEAD` receives 405 (HY-27). <a id="HY-62.34"></a> Then a request that selects `application/vnd.hyper+json` or a representation (HY-116) receives status 406 with the text `Not Acceptable` and `Vary: Accept`, and a request that selects `text/html` receives status 200 with the bytes of the shell as its body and the response of the application to it has the headers `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, the `Vary` of HY-117 and the frame policy of HY-45, and no other header; its host may add headers as HY-130 allows. <a id="HY-62.25"></a> The shell holds the element `hyper-build` of HY-125, which `hyper build` writes.

  <a id="HY-62.26"></a> The 405 and 406 responses and the shell response of a chosen request run no loader or action, read no session (HY-45), and contain no request data. <a id="HY-62.27"></a> Every response of a chosen request carries the frame policy of HY-45 and is reported to the response hook of HY-60. <a id="HY-62.39"></a> The open fails with kind `invalid_application` (HY-106.21) when the path of the shell file is not absolute, when the file does not exist or cannot be read, and when its bytes are not valid UTF-8. <a id="HY-62.36"></a> In Python the choice is `Choice(chosen, value)`, and a choice whose `chosen` is not a boolean is another value (HY-62.11) in the three servers. <a id="HY-62.37"></a> The message of a failure of HY-62.15 or HY-62.35 names its cause: the static shell with its path, the data base path, or the route that lies under the data base path. <a id="HY-62.38"></a> A request that HY-59.4 or HY-42 refuses calls no selection.

- **HYC-6** <a id="HYC-6.1"></a> When client-side rendering mounts a rendered document (HYC-8, HYC-3), the browser replaces the attributes of the `html` element with the attributes of the `html` element of the rendered document, in their order: an attribute that the rendered element does not have is removed. <a id="HYC-6.2"></a> A layout that renders `<html lang="{= language}">` therefore gives a client-rendered page the language of its data, as the server-rendered document has it. <a id="HYC-6.3"></a> The static shell that `scripts/build-assets.mjs` writes has no `lang` attribute, because it holds no data.

## Actions

- **HY-24** <a id="HY-24.1"></a> The session token is 32 random bytes that the server creates when the session first needs it. <a id="HY-24.2"></a> The value `csrf` of a response (HY-10) masks it: 32 random bytes `r` that the server draws once per response, followed by `r` XOR the token, written as 128 lowercase hexadecimal digits. <a id="HY-24.3"></a> Every response draws a new `r`, so no response contains the bytes of the token, and the compressed size of a response that also contains request input does not reveal it. <a id="HY-24.4"></a> An action request and a save of a kept value (HY-40) must contain the form field `_csrf` with a masked value of the session token: 128 lowercase hexadecimal digits whose second half XOR its first half equals the token, compared in constant time. <a id="HY-24.5"></a> Otherwise the server responds with status 403 and runs no action. <a id="HY-24.6"></a> The server never sends the token itself. <a id="HY-24.14"></a> A server holds the token as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, and a session that holds another value in the place of the token fails the request with kind `invalid_session_token` (HY-43), as a stored flash value or kept value of another form does (HY-104.23), because replacing it with a new token would turn a damaged record into a valid session; masking or verifying with a token or a mask in any other form fails with HY-43, while a form value that is not 128 lowercase hexadecimal digits is not valid (HY-24.5). <a id="HY-24.10"></a> A request that opens a session (HY-120) gives its handlers `browser()`: the SHA-256 digest of the 32 bytes of the session token, written as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, a value that names the browser of the request and from which the token cannot be computed. <a id="HY-24.15"></a> The server computes the value from the masked token that the request holds, so the value is the same for every request of one session until the token is replaced: when an action renews the session (HY-72), the action reads the digest of the old token and the handlers that run after it read the digest of the new token. <a id="HY-24.12"></a> A request that opens no session holds the empty text in the place of the masked token and has no such value, so its `browser()` returns null, in Python `None`: the request that a representation handler receives (HY-120.4) and a request that a host creates. <a id="HY-24.13"></a> A request whose masked token is neither the empty text nor 128 lowercase hexadecimal digits, which only a caller that creates a request by hand gives, fails `browser()` as masking with a token of another form does (HY-24.14).

- **HY-72** <a id="HY-72.1"></a> An action renews the session with `renewSession()` of its reply when the visitor that the session belongs to changes, such as at sign-in and sign-out. <a id="HY-72.2"></a> After the action returns, the server moves the session values to a new session identifier, deletes the old session, creates a new session token and sets the new session cookie; the flash values of a redirect and the kept values stay. <a id="HY-72.3"></a> A page that the action renders carries a masked value of the new token. <a id="HY-72.4"></a> A loader or the shared handler that calls `renewSession()` fails with HY-43, because the page that it renders carries the old token.

- **HY-25** <a id="HY-25.1"></a> An action that succeeds returns a redirect. <a id="HY-25.2"></a> The server responds with status 303 and `Location`, stores the flash values and the changed topics in the session, and removes them after the next request reads them. <a id="HY-25.3"></a> The browser follows the redirect with the same headers, and htmx records the final URL in history. <a id="HY-25.4"></a> The flash values of a result are values of the data model (HY-44): storing a value outside it fails when it is stored, with the error of the data model. <a id="HY-25.5"></a> A flash value stored again under its name replaces the value at the place of that name, and a changed topic recorded again keeps its first place. <a id="HY-25.7"></a> A flash name and a changed topic are strings: another value fails with kind `invalid_argument_type` of the binding in the three servers.

- **HY-26** <a id="HY-26.1"></a> An action that rejects its input returns invalid data. <a id="HY-26.2"></a> The server responds with status 422 and renders the route page with the route data merged with the invalid data, as JSON for a JSON request and as a document otherwise.

## Data

- **HYC-10** <a id="HYC-10.1"></a> The output of a region is a function of its template, the shared data and the region data. <a id="HYC-10.2"></a> The browser changes the page only by replacing region data and rendering it. <a id="HYC-10.3"></a> Form controls hold the values that a user is entering; every other screen state, such as a sort order or an open panel, is region data.

- **HY-30** <a id="HY-30.1"></a> A route may declare route regions, for example `"regions": [{ "name": "rows", "template": "board/rows.tpl" }]`. <a id="HY-30.2"></a> A part of a page that changes in the browser without a request to the application is a route region; the browser may load the template files that the change renders and that it has not loaded (HYC-12). <a id="HY-30.3"></a> The route template, or a template that it includes or places by path, places each route region with `{# name}`, without block arguments, inside an element whose `id` is the region name; `hyper check` fails when no template of that graph places a route region. <a id="HY-30.4"></a> A route region loader may return `null`, which makes the region absent from that response (HY-75). <a id="HY-30.5"></a> Region names are unique across the manifest regions and every route region. <a id="HY-30.6"></a> Each route region has its own loader. <a id="HY-30.7"></a> The page region receives every route region as HTML (HY-13), and every JSON response that contains the page region contains the route regions right after it.

- **HY-75** <a id="HY-75.1"></a> A route region is present in a response when its loader returns data, and absent when it returns `null`. <a id="HY-75.2"></a> An absent route region has no entry in `regions` of the JSON response, in the embedded data (HY-31) or in `kept`, and the page region receives no definition for it, so `{?# name}` is false; a template that places a route region that may be absent places its element inside `{?# name}…{/}`. <a id="HY-75.3"></a> A response carries no kept value of an absent region. <a id="HY-75.4"></a> The browser holds only the present route regions (HYC-4), so `data`, `render`, `set` and `hy-set` fail for an absent one (HYC-11). <a id="HY-75.5"></a> After it renders or swaps the page region, the browser checks that every present route region of the held route has exactly one element with its `id` in the page and that no absent route region has one; otherwise it sets `hy-error="0"` on the body (HYC-14). <a id="HY-75.6"></a> This lets a page that places views at request time under one route, such as a page that an administrator composes, declare a route region for a view that only some of its pages place. <a id="HY-75.7"></a> A route region without a loader is present with no data of its own.

- **HY-31** <a id="HY-31.1"></a> The layout places `{# data}` once, before `</body>`. <a id="HY-31.2"></a> The embedded data is the part of the document JSON value (HY-17) that the browser can change: `env`, `route`, `params`, `build`, `context` with `value` (HY-128) and `shared` as the JSON response has them (HY-73), `regions` with only the route regions of the route (HY-30) in their order, and `kept` with only the entries of those regions. <a id="HY-31.3"></a> A document embeds its data when the reply of its request asks for it (HY-92) and a route region of the route is present (HY-75): the definition `data` then renders the reserved template `hyper/data.tpl`, whose source is exactly `<script type="application/json" id="hy-data">{= json(response) | raw}</script>`, with `response` equal to the embedded data. <a id="HY-31.9"></a> One rule of the Rust core gives the name and the source of the reserved template, so that the build, which writes no copy of it below `program/templates/`, and every server take them from one place. <a id="HY-31.10"></a> While a server does not call the core, the build writes the copy `program/legacy/hyper/data.tpl` of that source, which only such a server reads. <a id="HY-31.4"></a> Otherwise the definition `data` is empty and the document has no `#hy-data`, so its source holds only the HTML of the page. <a id="HY-31.5"></a> A document of client-side rendering (HYC-8) never embeds its data, because the browser holds the data of the JSON response that it rendered. <a id="HY-31.6"></a> The PHP server and the Node server compute and render the embedded data the same way, so a document keeps the same bytes on both. <a id="HY-31.7"></a> A region request does not render it. <a id="HY-31.8"></a> A JSON response keeps every region (HY-18), because the browser renders them.

- **HY-92** <a id="HY-92.1"></a> A loader, an action or the shared handler of a request makes the HTML document of its response embed its data (HY-31) with `embedData()` of its reply (HY-52): `$reply->embedData()` in PHP, `reply.embedData()` in Node and `reply.embed_data()` in Python. <a id="HY-92.2"></a> Without the call a document embeds no data. <a id="HY-92.3"></a> The call changes no JSON response (HY-17), redirect or stop, and a request of client-side rendering (HY-62) receives the shell or JSON, which hold no embedded data. <a id="HY-92.4"></a> An application decides it per request, for example by the stored service of the host that its selection reads (HY-62).

- **HY-71** <a id="HY-71.1"></a> The data that the server sends is public to the visitor of the request. <a id="HY-71.2"></a> Shared data, region data and kept values reach the browser in the embedded data (HY-31), in every JSON response (HY-17) and in client-side rendering (HYC-8), so a value passed to a template does not stay on the server. <a id="HY-71.3"></a> A loader and the shared handler return only values that the visitor of the request may see: a value that the page does not show, such as a password hash, a session token or personal data that the visitor may not see, is never part of them. <a id="HY-71.4"></a> The server also removes every value that the templates do not read (HY-73), but that removal does not make a value safe to return. <a id="HY-71.5"></a> A value that the page shows reaches the browser in the HTML anyway. <a id="HY-71.6"></a> The masked CSRF token is shared data (HY-10, HY-24), because the browser sends it back with every form; the session token itself is never sent.

- **HY-73** <a id="HY-73.1"></a> The server sends only the data that the templates of a route read, except `context`, which it sends whole (HY-126). <a id="HY-73.2"></a> The read paths are computed from the template ASTs before any request, and they include at least every value that rendering reads, so rendering the kept data gives the same bytes as rendering the loader data.

  - <a id="HY-73.3"></a> A path is a list of steps from the root data: a map key, a list index written in decimal, or `*`, which stands for every entry of a map or every element of a list. <a id="HY-73.4"></a> A path read whole keeps its value as it is; a path read in part keeps only the paths below it that are read.
  - <a id="HY-73.5"></a> An expression has a set of paths. <a id="HY-73.6"></a> A variable has the root path of its name, together with the paths that a local variable of that name holds; a local variable holds the union of the paths of every assignment `{:x = e}` of its scope. <a id="HY-73.7"></a> The loop variable of `{@ v = e}` exists only in the body of that loop: there `v` has every path of `e` followed by `*` and the paths of the assignments to `v`, and neither its root path nor the paths of an outer loop variable of the same name. <a id="HY-73.8"></a> Outside the body the loop variable adds no path to `v`, so an assignment before the loop that reads the name of its loop variable, as in `{:p = page.x}{@ page = p.items}`, keeps the paths that it had before the loop. <a id="HY-73.9"></a> `v.value_` has the paths of `v`, and another loop meta field has none. <a id="HY-73.31"></a> A member, and an index whose key is a string or number literal, add the key to every path: a member its name, a string literal its text, and a number literal the number text of json, which writes the number as ECMAScript `Number::toString` does (RQ-030 of json), such as `1.5`, `1e+21`, `1e-7` and `123456789012345680`; a negative number is an operator on a literal, so its index is another index (HY-73.11). <a id="HY-73.11"></a> Another index reads its object and its key whole and has no path. <a id="HY-73.12"></a> `a ?? b` has the paths of `a` and `b`, a ternary the paths of its two results, and every other expression none.
  - <a id="HY-73.13"></a> An expression reads its paths whole when its value is output, is the test of `{? }`, `{:? }` or a ternary, is an operand of an operator other than `??`, is an argument of a function, a member call or a class call, the object of a member call, an item, key, value or spread of a list or map literal, or the key of an index. <a id="HY-73.14"></a> A loop `{@ v = e}` reads every path of `e` followed by `*` in part, so the loop keeps every entry.
  - <a id="HY-73.15"></a> An include `{+ path}` reads in the scope of the including template. <a id="HY-73.16"></a> A block with a path reads its template in a new scope, where the root names hold their root paths and every scope argument holds the paths of its expression in the calling scope; a block that places a template already being placed above it reads nothing, because rendering fails there (RT-22 of the template language). <a id="HY-73.17"></a> A block that places a definition reads nothing.
  - <a id="HY-73.18"></a> The read paths of the shared data of a route are those of the layout, the title, every manifest region template, the route template and every route region template, and `csrf` whole when a route region keeps a value on the server (HYC-13). <a id="HY-73.19"></a> The read paths of the data of a region are those of its template, the route template for the page region, and the kept paths of a route region whole. <a id="HY-73.20"></a> `hyper/data.tpl` reads nothing.
  - <a id="HY-73.29"></a> Before it renders or encodes a page, the server keeps of the shared data and of every region's data only their read paths: a map keeps the keys that a path names, in their order in the data, with their values kept recursively, and every key under `*`; a list keeps its length, with each element kept under `*` and the paths of its index and with `null` at an index that no path names; any other value stays as it is. <a id="HY-73.22"></a> A map that becomes empty stays a map.
  - <a id="HY-73.23"></a> The build writes the read paths of every route to `reads.json` of the server program (HY-48), and the Node server computes them with the browser package when the application opens. <a id="HY-73.30"></a> One rule of the Rust core computes the read paths of every route from the manifest and the sources of the templates, in the form of the routes of `reads.json` that the server reads when the application opens, and the read paths of one template. <a id="HY-73.32"></a> The routes of `reads.json` follow the manifest: each route, in manifest order, holds `shared` and then `regions`, which holds the manifest regions that have a template in manifest order, then the page region, then the route regions of the route in manifest order; a node holds `keys` before `each`, and the keys of `keys` follow the byte order of their UTF-8 text, so the bytes of `reads.json`, which the build id hashes (HY-125.15), depend only on the read paths. <a id="HY-73.25"></a> `data(region)` (HYC-11) returns the kept data, so a path that no template reads is not there.

  <a id="HY-73.28"></a> The kept data renders the same bytes as the data.

## Browser data

- **HYC-4** <a id="HYC-4.1"></a> The browser holds the data of the last response that it rendered: the environment, the route, the parameters, the shared data and the data of the route regions of the route (HY-30). <a id="HYC-4.2"></a> When a server-rendered page opens with `open()` of the browser code, and when htmx restores a page from history by requesting its HTML, the browser reads the embedded data from the element `#hy-data` (HY-31), replaces all held data with it and starts loading the templates of the route (HYC-12). <a id="HYC-4.3"></a> A document without `#hy-data` leaves no held data, and the browser obtains the data with HYC-7 when it first needs it. <a id="HYC-4.4"></a> It needs the data when the page opens only when a `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` value is stored for a kept path of a route region of the route (HY-37, HY-38), so a page that is only viewed and has no such value sends no request beyond its document. <a id="HYC-4.5"></a> A region response (HYC-2) replaces all held data with its own, because it contains the shared data, the page region and every present route region (HY-17, HY-18, HY-30), which is all that the browser holds. <a id="HYC-4.6"></a> The browser also holds the context of the application and the build of the page (HYC-22). <a id="HYC-4.7"></a> `render` (HYC-11) replaces held region data.
