- **HYC-7** <a id="HYC-7.1"></a> The browser obtains the data that it does not hold with one document request (HY-15) for the URL of the current page, its path and its query, with `Accept: application/vnd.hyper+json`. <a id="HYC-7.2"></a> It obtains the data when `data`, `render`, `set` or `hy-set` (HYC-11, HYC-5) names a route region of the route of the current page while it holds no data, and when the page opens with a stored browser kept value (HYC-4). <a id="HYC-7.3"></a> A call that names another region sends no request: `data` returns nothing, and the other calls fail. <a id="HYC-7.4"></a> Calls that need the data while the request is pending wait for the same request. <a id="HYC-7.5"></a> The response must be a JSON response with status 200 whose URL routes to the route of the current page (HYC-1). <a id="HYC-7.6"></a> The browser then applies the browser kept values (HY-38), holds the data and renders every present route region of the route from it as HY-38 renders the regions of an embedded document, so that the page shows the data that the browser holds, also when the data changed after the server rendered the HTML; the call then continues with the held data. <a id="HYC-7.7"></a> When a response (HYC-2, HYC-4) replaced the held data while the request was pending, the browser drops the response of the request, and the call continues with the held data. <a id="HYC-7.8"></a> Another response, a network failure or a response that cannot be decoded leaves no held data, marks the region of the call, or the body when the page opens, with the status of the response or `0` (HYC-14), and fails the call; the next call that needs the data sends the request again. <a id="HYC-7.9"></a> The request runs the loaders of the page again as its HTML request did, so a loader of a `GET` request changes no stored state (RFC 9110, section 9.2.1), and the page of an action that rendered in place (HY-26, HY-58, HY-69) receives the data of the `GET` request of its URL.

- **HYC-11** <a id="HYC-11.1"></a> The browser code provides `data(region)`, which returns a promise of the held data of a region; `render(region, data)`, which replaces the held data of a region; and `set(region, path, value)`, which replaces one value at a dotted path (map keys and list indexes) in the held data of a region. <a id="HYC-11.2"></a> The region is a route region of the held route (HY-30); another region fails. <a id="HYC-11.3"></a> A path that the data does not contain fails. <a id="HYC-11.4"></a> `render` and `set` then render the region alone (HY-13) and swap it into the region element with `innerMorph`. <a id="HYC-11.5"></a> The page region uses the template of the held route and the held route regions (HY-13). <a id="HYC-11.6"></a> These operations send no request, except the document request of HYC-7 while the browser holds no data. <a id="HYC-11.7"></a> There is no change tracking: the code that changes data asks for the rendering. <a id="HYC-11.8"></a> Calls run one after another in call order, and each starts from the held data that the previous call left. <a id="HYC-11.9"></a> A call checks the held data of its own region: when a response (HYC-4) replaced it before the swap, the call ends without swapping, holding or storing; when a response replaced it during the swap, the call does not hold or store and renders the region again from the held data. <a id="HYC-11.10"></a> A response that leaves the region unchanged does not affect the call.

- **HYC-5** <a id="HYC-5.1"></a> A template may give an element the attribute `hy-set="path=value; path=value"`, where each value is a JSON literal and each path follows HYC-11. <a id="HYC-5.2"></a> A click on the element, or on an element inside it, runs every assignment in the held data of the closest enclosing element whose `id` is the name of a route region of the held route, or of the route of the current page while the browser holds no data (HYC-7), and renders that region once. <a id="HYC-5.3"></a> The template computes the assigned values, for example `hy-set="service.close.flag={? service.close.flag}0{:}1{/}"`. <a id="HYC-5.4"></a> `hy-set` works only with JavaScript.

## Client stream subscription

- **HYC-17** <a id="HYC-17.1"></a> The TypeScript client `Hyper` of `packages/client` provides `subscribe(url, listener, options)`, which opens the event stream of `url` and returns a subscription with `close()`. <a id="HYC-17.2"></a> The request is made by the client's `options.fetch` (HyperOptions `fetch`; the global `fetch` when the option is absent) with method `GET`, the header `Accept: text/event-stream` and `credentials: 'same-origin'`, as the document requests of HYC-7 are made. <a id="HYC-17.3"></a> The listener has `onEvent(event)`, which receives each event with its `event`, `data` and `id` (HYC-18), and `onError(error)`, which receives each failure of HYC-20. <a id="HYC-17.4"></a> The options are `watchdogMs` (HYC-20). <a id="HYC-17.5"></a> `subscribe` throws when the client is disposed (HYC-21) and when `watchdogMs` is not a positive finite number. <a id="HYC-17.6"></a> This subscription is carried only by the TypeScript client; the PHP, Python and Node servers have no client, and no other client of this repository has a stream.

- **HYC-18** <a id="HYC-18.1"></a> The body of the response is read as a WHATWG HTML "server-sent events" event stream: the fields `data`, `event`, `id` and `retry`, the lines ended by CRLF, LF or CR, the lines that begin with `:` as comments, and an event dispatched at each blank line. <a id="HYC-18.2"></a> The `event` of an event is its `event` field, or `message` when it has none, and its `data` is the `data` fields of the event joined by LF. <a id="HYC-18.3"></a> The `id` of an event is the last event ID that the standard keeps: the value of the last `id` field that the stream sent, which an event without an `id` field also carries. <a id="HYC-18.4"></a> An `id` or `retry` field whose value is invalid, and a field with an unknown name, are ignored, as the standard says, and are not failures. <a id="HYC-18.5"></a> The implementation parses the stream with the npm package `eventsource-parser`, not with a hand-written parser: the line endings, the byte-order mark and the incomplete last line of the standard are what that maintained parser already implements (S1). <a id="HYC-18.6"></a> The package is the choice of this rule for the TypeScript client, and its exact version is pinned with its reason in `docs/operations/dependencies.md` when the implementation row of HYC-17 is done. <a id="HYC-18.7"></a> A body that is not valid UTF-8 is a parse failure: the implementation decodes the body with a fatal decoder, and the failure is an error of HYC-20.

- **HYC-19** <a id="HYC-19.1"></a> The subscription keeps the last event ID and the retry delay, as the standard does. <a id="HYC-19.2"></a> The last event ID is the `id` of the last event that had an `id` field, and it is kept across reconnections; the retry delay is the value of the last `retry` field, in milliseconds, and defaults to 1000 when the server sent none. <a id="HYC-19.3"></a> When the stream ends, fails with an error of HYC-20, or answers with a status other than 2xx, the client reports the failure to `onError` and then reconnects after the retry delay. <a id="HYC-19.4"></a> The reconnection request carries the header `Last-Event-ID` with the last event ID when it is not empty, and carries no other cursor: no query parameter or other header states the position of the stream. <a id="HYC-19.5"></a> The 1000 ms default bounds the reconnection rate of a client whose server states no delay. <a id="HYC-19.6"></a> The client reconnects until `close()` or `dispose()` (HYC-21).

- **HYC-20** <a id="HYC-20.1"></a> The subscription has a byte watchdog. <a id="HYC-20.2"></a> When no byte of the body arrives for `watchdogMs` milliseconds, the stream fails with an error whose cause names the URL and the time, and the client then reconnects (HYC-19). <a id="HYC-20.3"></a> The watchdog restarts with each byte, and counts bytes, not events, so a stream that sends bytes without a complete event does not fail. <a id="HYC-20.4"></a> The default of `watchdogMs` is 30000: a silent connection then fails before the 60 s idle timeout that common reverse proxies apply by default, which would close it without telling the client. <a id="HYC-20.5"></a> Every failure of a subscription is reported to `onError` with its cause: a watchdog timeout, a non-2xx response (with its status and URL), a network failure, and a parse failure of HYC-18. <a id="HYC-20.6"></a> No failure is dropped silently (P8). <a id="HYC-20.7"></a> A close or a dispose is not a failure and reports nothing.

- **HYC-21** <a id="HYC-21.1"></a> `dispose()` of the client aborts every subscription and every pending request. <a id="HYC-21.2"></a> For each subscription it aborts the request, clears the watchdog timer and the retry timer, and sets the subscription closed; it aborts every pending region request and document request of the client (HYC-3, HYC-7). <a id="HYC-21.3"></a> After `dispose()` returns, the client has no timer running and calls no listener, and a response that arrives later is discarded. <a id="HYC-21.4"></a> `dispose()` may be called more than once; a call after the first has no effect. <a id="HYC-21.5"></a> A `subscribe` after `dispose()` throws, so that no subscription starts after the client is disposed.

## Template delivery

- **HYC-12** <a id="HYC-12.1"></a> The browser loads a template when rendering reaches it. <a id="HYC-12.2"></a> It renders, and when the rendering requested templates that are not loaded, it loads each of them by its index URL and renders again, until the rendering completes or fails for another reason. <a id="HYC-12.3"></a> A template that no rendering reaches, such as the template of a branch that the data does not select, is not loaded, so a route whose template selects one of many views loads only the views that it shows. <a id="HYC-12.4"></a> The entry templates of a route are the layout, the title, every non-page region template, the route template and every route region template; for a region request the browser starts loading them with the request, at the same time, and when the response URL routes to another route, such as after a redirect, it loads the entry templates of that route. <a id="HYC-12.5"></a> When a server-rendered page opens, the browser loads no template; it loads the templates that it needs when it first renders a region of that page. <a id="HYC-12.6"></a> The browser never renders `hyper/data.tpl`, because a client-rendered document embeds no data (HY-31); the Node server, which renders it, checks that the index holds it. <a id="HYC-12.7"></a> A name that the index does not hold fails the rendering (HYC-14). <a id="HYC-12.8"></a> Loaded templates stay loaded until the page unloads. <a id="HYC-12.9"></a> The Node server, which renders every page, reads every template of the index when it opens.

- **HYC-16** <a id="HYC-16.1"></a> A page requests only the resources that it uses, and each resource at most once while the page is loaded. <a id="HYC-16.2"></a> A resource is a template file, a stylesheet or a script file. <a id="HYC-16.3"></a> The browser loads a template when rendering reaches it (HYC-12). <a id="HYC-16.4"></a> The layout links only the stylesheets of the content that it renders, and the browser applies the stylesheet links of each rendered head and keeps a link that is already applied (HYC-15); a stylesheet that the application links on every page is one that every page uses. <a id="HYC-16.10"></a> The layout names only the module scripts of the content that it renders, and the browser creates each module script of a rendered head once and removes none (HYC-25); a module script that the layout names on every page is one that every page uses. <a id="HYC-16.5"></a> `hyper build` writes the client entry `public/assets/hyper-<hash>.js` and, for code that the entry imports with `import()` and does not import statically, chunk files `public/assets/hyper-chunk-<hash>.js`; the browser loads a chunk when that code first runs, by an absolute URL below `/assets/`, so the entry that the static shell inlines loads it too, and the browser loads a module once. <a id="HYC-16.12"></a> The build gives every file that it writes below `public/assets` a name that holds a hash of its content: the template files and the index (HR-34), the entry, its chunks and the assets of `--asset` and `--tailwind` (HR-77), and it writes `client/manifest.json` into `--output`, whose member `hyper` is the URL of the entry and whose member `<name>` is the URL of the asset of that name, and the static shell. <a id="HYC-16.13"></a> An asset name matches `[a-z][a-z0-9-]*` and is neither `hyper` nor starts with `hyper-`, because `hyper` is the member of the entry and the entry and its chunks own the names that start with `hyper-`, and the build fails before it writes any output when a name breaks that form or two assets of one build have the same name. <a id="HYC-16.7"></a> The application places and links its own stylesheets and names with `--static` the files below `public/` that the static deployment holds at the same path, such as the stylesheets that its layouts link; the build adds no other file of `public/assets` to the deployment than the files that it writes, because `public/assets` keeps the files of earlier builds. <a id="HYC-16.8"></a> The static shell contains `<meta name="hyper-api">`, the inlined entry and no stylesheet, because the browser applies the stylesheet links of the rendered layout before it shows the page (HYC-8, HYC-15). <a id="HYC-16.11"></a> The static shell also contains `<meta name="hyper-entry" content="/assets/hyper-<hash>.js">`, whose content is the member `hyper` of `client/manifest.json`, the URL of the entry that it inlines, because an inlined script has no address and a layout that names the entry as a module script must not load it again (HYC-25). <a id="HYC-16.9"></a> `tests/scripts/build-assets.test.mts` builds an application whose entry imports a module with `import()`.

## Kept data

- **HY-37** <a id="HY-37.1"></a> A route region may declare kept paths, because only route regions change in the browser (HY-30); the manifest check rejects `keep` on a manifest region. <a id="HY-37.2"></a> An example is `"keep": { "notice.closed": "server", "sort": "localStorage" }`. <a id="HY-37.3"></a> A path is a dotted path: a map key `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, then any number of `.` each followed by a map key or by a list index of decimal digits. <a id="HY-37.4"></a> A kept value survives a reload in the storage named by its kind:

| Kind | Storage | Request when the value changes | First SSR document |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `server` | the server session | one background request that rendering does not wait for | contains the value |
| `cookie` | the cookie `hy-keep`, written by the browser code; it cannot be `HttpOnly` | none | contains the value |
| `localStorage` | the browser `localStorage` | none | contains the loader value; the browser renders the kept value after it loads |
| `sessionStorage` | the browser `sessionStorage` of the tab | none | contains the loader value; the browser renders the kept value after it loads |

- **HY-38** <a id="HY-38.1"></a> The value that the user set last in the browser takes precedence; the loader data is the default. <a id="HY-38.2"></a> A kept value conforms to the value at its path when the region data contains the path, the kept value is a value of the template data model (a number outside ±(2^53 − 1) is not), and:

  - <a id="HY-38.3"></a> a null, boolean, number or string has the same type;
  - <a id="HY-38.4"></a> a map replaces a map; when the data map has keys, the kept map has the same keys and the value of every key conforms to the value of the same key;
  - <a id="HY-38.5"></a> a list replaces a list; when the data list has items, every kept item conforms to its first item.

  <a id="HY-38.6"></a> An empty data map or list gives no shape, so any map or list conforms to it; the rendering check below covers such values.

  <a id="HY-38.7"></a> A kept value that does not conform is ignored.

  - <a id="HY-38.8"></a> The server reads `server` and `cookie` values and sends the conforming ones in `kept` (HY-17). <a id="HY-38.9"></a> They never change `regions`. <a id="HY-38.10"></a> It reads the `cookie` values from the cookie `__Host-hy-keep` when the request uses HTTPS or the application declares HTTPS (HY-45), and from `hy-keep` otherwise; on HTTPS the host-only cookie alone counts, because another host, such as a sibling subdomain, cannot set it. <a id="HY-38.11"></a> The cookie value is the URL-encoded JSON object `{ "<region>": { "<path>": <value> } }`.
  - <a id="HY-38.12"></a> A region renders with its kept values applied to its data in this order: the values in `kept`, the `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` values, and the `server` values whose saving has not completed (HYC-13). <a id="HY-38.13"></a> The server applies only the values in `kept`. <a id="HY-38.14"></a> The browser applies all of them to the data that it holds and renders, and does not synchronize them with the server. <a id="HY-38.15"></a> For a document rendered by the server, the browser applies them after it holds the embedded data, or after it obtains the data when a browser value is stored (HYC-4, HYC-7), and renders every region whose data changed.
  - <a id="HY-38.16"></a> When a region does not render alone (HY-13) with its kept values applied, it renders with its loader data, and its kept values are removed from `kept` and from the held data. <a id="HY-38.17"></a> The server removes them before it renders the embedded data (HY-31), so the server and the browser render the same document. <a id="HY-38.18"></a> When the region does not render with its loader data either, rendering fails (HY-43, HYC-14).

  <a id="HY-38.19"></a> A kept value takes the place of the value at its path, so every map of the data keeps its keys in their order, and a kept map keeps its keys in its own order.

- **HYC-13** <a id="HYC-13.1"></a> When `set`, `render` or `hy-set` changes a path, the browser renders the region first and then stores every kept path that equals the changed path, lies under it or contains it, with the value now at the kept path. <a id="HYC-13.2"></a> A `server` value stays pending until the server answers 204 for it or a later change of the same path is saved; while it is pending it is applied as in HY-38. <a id="HYC-13.3"></a> Saves of one path are sent one at a time: a change made while a save of its path is in flight is sent after that save completes, and only the latest value is sent. <a id="HYC-13.4"></a> A failed save keeps the value pending and marks the region as failed (HYC-14) when no later change of the path exists. <a id="HYC-13.5"></a> For `server` it sends `POST <base path>/_hyper/keep` with the form fields `_csrf` (the held `shared.csrf`, HY-10), `region`, `path` and `value` (the JSON text of the value) and does not wait for the response. <a id="HYC-13.6"></a> For `cookie` it writes the cookie `hy-keep` with `Path=/`, `SameSite=Lax` and `Max-Age` of one year; on HTTPS the cookie is `__Host-hy-keep` and also `Secure`, so that another host, such as a sibling subdomain, cannot set it. <a id="HYC-13.7"></a> The cookie value is the URL-encoded JSON object `{ "<region>": { "<path>": <value> } }`.

- **HY-40** <a id="HY-40.1"></a> The server answers `POST <base path>/_hyper/keep` with status 204 after it stores the value in the session, with status 403 when the CSRF token does not match, and with status 400 when the region does not declare the path as `server`, the value is not JSON, the JSON text is longer than 4,096 bytes, or the value is not a value of the template data model. <a id="HY-40.2"></a> The path `/_hyper/keep` is reserved; a route path may not start with `/_hyper`. <a id="HY-40.3"></a> The kept values of a region that stored none are an empty map. <a id="HY-40.4"></a> A kept value that the session stores is a value of the data model (HY-44): storing a value outside it fails when it is stored, with the error of the data model, as a flash value does (HY-25.4).

## Request boundary and failures

- **HY-42** <a id="HY-42.1"></a> The request path is the path of the request target: the target up to its first `?` or `#`, and for an absolute-form target (`http://host/path`) the part after the authority. <a id="HY-42.2"></a> It is not decoded further. <a id="HY-42.3"></a> The path must consist of the printable ASCII characters `!` to `~`, as RFC 9112 requires of a request target, and every query and form name and value (HY-56, HY-57) and the `HX-Current-URL` header must be valid UTF-8; otherwise the server responds with status 400 before any loader or action runs. <a id="HY-42.4"></a> Cookies are not checked: the server ignores a `hy-keep` cookie that is not a JSON object, ignores its values that do not conform (HY-38), and starts a new session for a session cookie that is not an identifier that it created (HY-45). <a id="HY-42.5"></a> A leading U+FEFF of a decoded query or form name or value (HY-56), of a route parameter (HY-5) and of a cookie value (HY-129) is a character of it, which no server and no browser code removes. <a id="HY-42.7"></a> The path, the raw query and the header names and values that a host gives a request are text whose characters U+0000 to U+00FF are its bytes, and a character above U+00FF in one of them fails with kind `invalid_text` of the binding, of the category `value`, while a PHP string holds bytes.

- **HY-43** <a id="HY-43.1"></a> An exception that the application does not handle produces status 500 with the text `Internal Server Error`. <a id="HY-43.2"></a> The response contains no exception message, file path or stack trace; the server writes them to its log. <a id="HY-43.3"></a> The PHP setting `display_errors` must be off before PHP starts the request, because PHP writes startup warnings (for example `max_input_vars`) before the application runs. <a id="HY-43.4"></a> The log is `error_log` in the PHP server, the standard error in the Python server, and in the Node server the function `log` of `App.open`, which writes to the standard error when the application gives none. <a id="HY-43.5"></a> The text that a server gives to its log for an unhandled error starts with `hyper: ` and contains the message of the error; the rest of the line is the runtime's. <a id="HY-43.6"></a> An exception of Python that is not an `Exception`, such as `SystemExit`, `KeyboardInterrupt` or `GeneratorExit`, ends the process or the task and is not an error of the application: the Python server closes the session of the request and lets the exception pass to its caller, and it writes no response and no log line and calls no hook for it.

- **HY-74** <a id="HY-74.1"></a> While a server answers a request, a warning that its runtime raises becomes an error, and the request fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-74.2"></a> The runtime would otherwise continue, and the server would send a wrong page with status 200 while the message reaches only the log or the output. <a id="HY-74.3"></a> An error that an expression silences stays silent. <a id="HY-74.4"></a> The server installs its handling for the requests only and restores the previous handling afterwards.

  - <a id="HY-74.5"></a> PHP: every warning, notice and deprecation that PHP raises, such as an undefined variable, an undefined array key or a wrong argument, becomes an exception through an error handler; an error that `@` silences is not in `error_reporting()` and stays silent.
  - <a id="HY-74.6"></a> Python: every warning of the `warnings` module that is raised while a request is answered, such as a `DeprecationWarning` or a `RuntimeWarning`, is raised as an exception: the filter `error` is set while a request is in flight.
  - <a id="HY-74.7"></a> Node: a warning that is emitted with `process.emitWarning` while a request is answered throws its error at the call.

- **HY-44** <a id="HY-44.1"></a> Shared data and region data are values of the template data model. <a id="HY-44.2"></a> A number outside ±(2^53 − 1), integer or not, fails with HY-43, for a document and for JSON alike. <a id="HY-44.3"></a> The server checks every value that the context handler (HY-124), the shared handler and the loaders return before it removes the values that no template reads (HY-73), so a value outside the data model fails also when no template reads it. <a id="HY-44.4"></a> The context handler (HY-124), the shared handler and every loader return a map: in PHP an array that is empty or is not a list, in Python a `dict`, and in Node a `Map` for the context handler and a plain object or a `Map` for the shared handler and every loader. <a id="HY-44.5"></a> Another value, such as a list, fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-44.6"></a> The check is the host binding of the template data model (VAL-13, VAL-14) followed by a check that the bound value holds no native object (VAL-19): a value that binding turns into a value of the data model passes, such as a PHP `stdClass` or `JsonSerializable` and a Node plain object, and an application object that binding keeps as a native object, such as a PHP `DateTimeImmutable`, a Node `Date` or a Python `datetime`, fails with HY-43 on every server. <a id="HY-44.7"></a> A JSON response checks only the parameters of the request again, because this check covered the shared data and the region data and a kept value enters a response only when it is a value of the data model (HY-38). <a id="HY-44.9"></a> A value outside the data model fails with the error of the template data model, whose kind, such as `data_number_range`, `data_number_not_finite`, `data_invalid_utf8`, `data_depth` or `data_unsupported_type`, and message hyper passes on as they are (VAL-2, VAL-3, VAL-13, VAL-20).

- **HY-45** <a id="HY-45.1"></a> The server session cookie is named `__Host-hy-session` when the request uses HTTPS or when the application declares that it is served over HTTPS, which a server behind a TLS-terminating proxy must do, and `hy-session` otherwise; the application does not choose the name. <a id="HY-45.2"></a> The browser accepts a `__Host-` cookie only from its own host, so another host, such as a sibling subdomain, cannot give a visitor a session whose token it knows. <a id="HY-45.3"></a> The cookie has `Path=/`, no `Domain`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`, and it is `Secure` under the same condition as the prefix. <a id="HY-45.4"></a> The server accepts only session identifiers that it created, and starts a session only when a request reads or writes session data: a request that the server rejects before routing (HY-42) or whose path matches no route creates no session. <a id="HY-45.5"></a> Every response carries `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <sources>`, where the application sets the sources and the default is `'self'`. <a id="HY-45.6"></a> A request uses HTTPS when its host states it: the TLS socket of `node:http`, `HTTPS` of the SAPI, `wsgi.url_scheme` of WSGI and `scheme` of ASGI; the `http.server` server states none, so there only the declaration of the application counts. <a id="HY-45.8"></a> Every server writes the session cookie with `set_cookie` of http-cookie (CK-6 to CK-12), with the path `/`, `secure` under the condition of HY-45.1, `http_only`, `same_site` `Lax` and no `Max-Age`, so its field value is `<name>=<id>; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`, with `; Secure` only under that condition (CK-9).

- **HY-46** <a id="HY-46.1"></a> A redirect location is an application path: valid UTF-8 that starts with `/`, whose second character is neither `/` nor `\`, that contains no control character (C0, DEL or C1), no space and no `\`, and whose path has no segment `.` or `..`, also when a dot is percent-encoded (`%2e`). <a id="HY-46.3"></a> Making a redirect to a location that is not an application path fails with kind `not_application_path` and the message `a redirect location is not an application path (HY-46)`, in the class of the category `value` (HY-132.2).

- **HYC-14** <a id="HYC-14.1"></a> When a region request receives a response that is not JSON, or when rendering, saving a kept value, loading templates, loading a stylesheet (HYC-15) or loading a module script (HYC-25) fails, the browser does not swap and does not change history. <a id="HYC-14.2"></a> It sets the attribute `hy-error` on the region element to the response status, or to `0` for a network or rendering failure, and removes the attribute from every region that renders successfully afterwards. <a id="HYC-14.3"></a> A cancelled request is not a failure; a request that htmx aborts because its timeout (`hx-timeout`, or `htmx.config.defaultTimeout`) passed is a network failure. <a id="HYC-14.4"></a> `render`, `set` and `hy-set` change held data only after the region rendered; a failure leaves held data unchanged. <a id="HYC-14.5"></a> When client-side rendering of a document fails, or a stylesheet or a module script of a history restoration in server-side rendering fails to load, the browser sets `hy-error` on the body.

- **HY-129** <a id="HY-129.13"></a> The cookies of a request are what `parse` of http-cookie gives for its `Cookie` field lines (CK-2 to CK-5), the same in every server: an ordered map from names to values, where the first cookie of a name counts and a pair that gives no cookie changes nothing. <a id="HY-129.14"></a> A host passes the field values of the `Cookie` lines that it received, in order, and does not join them (CK-2.4): the Node host takes the `Cookie` lines of `rawHeaders` of `node:http`, the Python `create_server` reads every `Cookie` line and the Python ASGI callable passes the `cookie` headers of the scope. <a id="HY-129.15"></a> A host whose runtime gives the lines already joined passes that value as one line: PHP takes `$_SERVER['HTTP_COOKIE']` from its SAPI, and the Python WSGI callable takes `HTTP_COOKIE` and encodes it in Latin-1 back to its bytes. <a id="HY-129.6"></a> The PHP built-in server joins several HTTP/1.1 `Cookie` lines with `, `, so such a request, which breaks RFC 6265 section 5.4, gives the cookies of that joined value. <a id="HY-129.16"></a> No part of the PHP server reads `$_COOKIE`, whose names PHP changes as the names of its variables (`a.b` becomes `a_b`, and `a[x]` an array): it receives the identifier of HY-45 from the parse of HY-129.13 and sends the session cookie of HY-45 itself.

- **HY-130** <a id="HY-130.19"></a> A response of an application carries the headers that the rules of this document name for it, and may carry other headers unless a rule states that it has no other header; the host of a server may add headers to any response. <a id="HY-130.20"></a> A header name has no case: names that differ only in ASCII case are one name (RFC 9110 section 5.1).

## Node server

- **HY-54** <a id="HY-54.22"></a> `server` is the role of this document and no package name: the server library of every language is the package of the main specification and carries the name of the repository, Composer `polyspec/hyper`, PyPI `polyspec-hyper`, npm `@polyspec/hyper` and the crate `polyspec-hyper` of its Rust core, and the browser package is `@polyspec/hyper-client`. <a id="HY-54.1"></a> The Node server package `@polyspec/hyper` implements the server rules of this document as the PHP server does; its tests run the cases of the PHP server tests against the same fixtures. <a id="HY-54.2"></a> It differs from the PHP server only as follows:

  - <a id="HY-54.3"></a> It renders a document as the browser renders the document JSON value (HY-12, HY-31, HY-38), with the browser code and the template files of `hyper build` (HR-34), and embeds its data when the reply asks for it (HY-92).
  - <a id="HY-54.18"></a> Every server writes JSON text with the serializer of json, the one JSON serializer of polyspec (RQ-011, RQ-034), and writes each number of the data model as VAL-9 of the template data model states, which is the number token of RQ-030, so the text of a value is the same bytes in every runtime. <a id="HY-54.19"></a> A string escapes `"`, `\` and the control characters U+0000 to U+001F, the characters that RFC 8259, section 7, requires to escape, and no other character, as the string writer of json does (RQ-028), so U+2028 and U+2029 are written as themselves. <a id="HY-54.20"></a> A server reads a JSON text, such as a kept value (HY-38, HY-40) or the body of a representation request (HY-121), with `parse` of json, which takes UTF-8 bytes (RQ-026, RQ-007) and refuses a text with more than 256 nested containers (RQ-006, RQ-035), and converts its value to the data model as VAL-12 of the template data model states, so a number outside ±(2^53 − 1) or not finite (VAL-2), a string that is not UTF-8 text, an escaped lone surrogate included, and a value deeper than 64 levels (VAL-20) fail with the error of the data model. <a id="HY-54.21"></a> A text that json refuses fails with kind `malformed_json`, whose source is the rejection of json with its kind and byte offset (RQ-004, RQ-005, RQ-033), and the reading limit of 256 and the depth of 64 of the data model are two limits with two kinds, because a text deeper than 256 levels is refused before it gives a value.
  - <a id="HY-54.12"></a> A JavaScript value of the data model is null, a boolean, a number or a bigint within ±(2^53 − 1), a string, an array, a `Map` with string keys or a plain object. <a id="HY-54.13"></a> A string with a lone surrogate, which has no UTF-8 form, and any other value fail with HY-43.
  - <a id="HY-54.14"></a> Loaders and actions receive one context argument with the request, the reply (HY-52) and the services that the application binds by key.
  - <a id="HY-54.15"></a> Its session store keeps each session in a file of one directory, named by an identifier of 64 hexadecimal digits that the store created. <a id="HY-54.17"></a> It runs the requests of one session one after another (HY-104).

- **HY-97** <a id="HY-97.1"></a> Every server takes an optional request hook `around`: an argument of `create_server`, `create_wsgi` and `create_asgi` (Python), an option of `listener` and `server` (Node), and an argument of `App::open` (PHP). <a id="HY-97.2"></a> The server calls it once for every request that it gives to the application, with the request as the server built it and a function `answer`, and sends the response that `around` returns. <a id="HY-97.3"></a> `answer(request)` runs the application for a request as the server does without `around`: it calls `App.handle` with the request and the session store of the server; `App.handle` opens the session of the request by its session cookie as HY-120 states, calls the response hook (HY-60) and closes the session, and `answer` returns the response with the cookie of a new session first (HY-45). <a id="HY-97.4"></a> `around` may call `answer` with the request or with a changed copy, such as a copy with a header that `Request.with_header(name, value)` (Python), `request.withHeader(name, value)` (Node) or `Request::withHeader($name, $value)` (PHP) sets (the name is compared without case, as a request reads a header); it may change the response that `answer` returns; and it may return its own response without calling `answer`, and then the server opens no session and runs no loader, action or hook of the application for that request. <a id="HY-97.5"></a> When a write of the response fails because the client closed the connection (HY-67), the server calls the disconnect hook with the request and the reply of the last call of `answer`, and does not call it when `around` did not call `answer`. <a id="HY-97.6"></a> The files of the public directory, which the Python and Node servers serve, are served before `around` and do not reach it. <a id="HY-97.7"></a> A value of `around` that is not callable fails when the server is created. <a id="HY-97.8"></a> An error that `around` raises outside `answer`, and a return value that is not a response, are escaped errors (HY-60), also for PHP, where `run` writes the plain 500 of an uncaught exception: the server logs them and answers the plain 500, which the write hook receives (HY-99). <a id="HY-97.11"></a> The copy holds every other part of the request, and the request is not changed. <a id="HY-97.12"></a> The failure of a return value of `around` that is no response contains the text `not a Response`.

  - <a id="HY-97.9"></a> The Node server gives the same through the `node:http` server that `app.server()` returns: a consumer replaces its `request` listener with a listener that calls the listener of the application, so that it runs each request in a context of its own, adds a request id header to the request and the response, or answers a request itself before the application, such as a 400 for a request that did not come from its web server. <a id="HY-97.10"></a> `around` gives these to an application of the Python server, whose `http.server` request handler is not replaceable.

- **HY-99** <a id="HY-99.1"></a> Every server takes an optional write hook `written`: an argument of `create_server`, `create_wsgi` and `create_asgi` (Python), an option of `listener` and `server` (Node), and an argument of `App::open` (PHP). <a id="HY-99.2"></a> The server calls it exactly once for each request that it gives to the application, with these values: the request that it gave to `around` (HY-97), or the request as received; the `Response` whose write it started, the plain 500 of an escaped error when none started, or null when the request ended before a response started; `ended`, which says whether the status line, the headers and the complete body were written without an error; the elapsed milliseconds since the arrival of the request (HY-60); and `failure`, the message of an escaped error as HY-43 states it, or null for every other response. <a id="HY-99.3"></a> It calls the hook after the answer of the request has ended (the application returned, failed or stopped on a closed connection, HY-67) and after the write ended or failed, whichever is later, and before the disconnect hook. <a id="HY-99.4"></a> An escaped error whose 500 cannot be written, because the response has started or the connection is closed, is reported with `ended` false and its failure. <a id="HY-99.5"></a> No adapter reports the plain 500 of an escaped error to the response hook. <a id="HY-99.6"></a> PHP calls the hook from a shutdown function that `run` registers after its escape function; `ended` is false when `connection_aborted()` is 1 or a fatal error ended the script after the headers were sent, and true means that PHP gave the complete output to the web server. <a id="HY-99.7"></a> Under either output buffering mode, `ended` and the response follow what PHP sent: with output buffering on and no output flushed, a fatal error after `run` replaces the response with the plain 500, which the hook receives with `ended` true; with output buffering off, or after a flush that sent the headers, the hook receives the started response with `ended` false. <a id="HY-99.8"></a> Node calls it after the `close` event of the `node:http` response and the end of the answer, with `ended` equal to `writableFinished`; the listener that `listener(app, sessions, options)` returns, which `server` installs, returns a promise that settles after the write hook and the disconnect hook of the request have run. <a id="HY-99.9"></a> WSGI: `ended` is true when the server consumes the whole body iterable, and false when it calls `close` before the end, also before the first item; an error before `start_response` is an escaped error, and so is a `start_response` that raises. <a id="HY-99.10"></a> ASGI: `ended` is true when both sends return, and false when a send raises or the task is cancelled; the error or the cancellation propagates. <a id="HY-99.11"></a> A request that ends before a response started, because its connection closed (HY-67), its task was cancelled (HY-100), or PHP `exit()` ended it without output, gives the hook a null response, with `ended` false and a null `failure` unless an error escaped. <a id="HY-99.12"></a> The hook is not called in three cases: for the files of the public directory, for a request that the transport gives no request to report (HY-60), and when the process ends before the request ends (a kill, or a worker timeout that ends the worker), because no code of the server runs then. <a id="HY-99.13"></a> An error that the hook raises is not handled by HY-43; it reaches the transport. <a id="HY-99.14"></a> A write hook that is not callable fails when the server is created, in Node and Python. <a id="HY-99.15"></a> For the response of `around` alone on a connection that the client closed, the hook receives that response with `ended` false in the three servers. <a id="HY-99.16"></a> The 400 and 431 responses of HY-60.7 call no write hook.

- **HY-100** <a id="HY-100.1"></a> Every server is served through the standard host interface of its runtime, and a host answers each request as the server does (HY-97, HY-99): PHP through a front controller that calls `run` under a SAPI (the built-in server or php-fpm), Python through the WSGI callable of `create_wsgi`, the ASGI callable of `create_asgi` or the `http.server` server of `create_server`, and Node through the `node:http` request listener of `listener`, which `server` installs. <a id="HY-100.2"></a> A host reads the request body up to the body limit of the application and no more (HY-59), passes its session store to `App.handle`, which opens the session as HY-120 states, sets the cookie of a new session first (HY-45), runs the request hook `around` (HY-97), reports the write to the write hook (HY-99) and a closed connection to the disconnect hook (HY-67), and answers a request whose target it cannot give with the plain 500 of HY-60. <a id="HY-100.31"></a> A host passes every request method that its transport accepts to the application in upper case, so such a method that no route allows receives the 405 of HY-27; `node:http` refuses a method outside its own list, and a method in lower case, with the 400 of HY-60.7. <a id="HY-100.32"></a> The HTTP version of the status line is the host's. <a id="HY-100.33"></a> The built-in server of PHP answers a method outside its own list with its 501 and closes the connection of a method in lower case without a response, so neither reaches the application.

  - <a id="HY-100.3"></a> Python WSGI: `create_wsgi(app, sessions, files=None, around=None, written=None)` of the package `polyspec.hyper` of the Python server `polyspec-hyper` takes the arguments of `create_server` (HY-97, HY-99) and returns a WSGI application callable (PEP 3333) that a WSGI server runs. <a id="HY-100.4"></a> The callable answers every request as `create_server` does: it serves the files of the public directory before `around`, reads the request body up to the body limit of the application and no more (HY-59), passes its session store to `App.handle`, which opens the session as HY-120 states, sets the cookie of a new session first (HY-45) and runs the request hook `around` (HY-97). <a id="HY-100.5"></a> It adds the header `Content-Length` of the complete body itself. <a id="HY-100.6"></a> The write hook `written` (HY-99) reports that the write ended when the WSGI server consumed the whole body iterable, and that it failed when the server closed the iterable before its end, which PEP 3333 defines as premature termination; when the write failed, the callable calls the disconnect hook (HY-67) with the request that it gave to `around` and the reply of the last call of `answer`. <a id="HY-100.7"></a> The hook is not called for the files of the public directory. <a id="HY-100.8"></a> An error that `around` raises outside `answer`, or a value that it returns that is not a `Response`, is an escaped error (HY-60): the callable answers the plain 500 before it calls `start_response`, and the write hook receives it. <a id="HY-100.9"></a> An error that `start_response` raises, and a status, a header or a body that the callable cannot encode, is an escaped error too: the callable passes the plain 500 to `start_response` with the exception information of the error (PEP 3333), and the write hook receives it with its `failure`. <a id="HY-100.10"></a> The request target is the one that the WSGI server received. <a id="HY-100.11"></a> PEP 3333 has no raw path, so the callable reads the target from `RAW_URI` (gunicorn) or else from `REQUEST_URI` (uWSGI, mod_wsgi). <a id="HY-100.12"></a> The request path is the target up to its first `?`, and the raw query is the text after its first `?` (HY-42, HY-56), split as `create_server` splits its target. <a id="HY-100.13"></a> The callable never reads `PATH_INFO`, which the server has percent-decoded, and never re-encodes it. <a id="HY-100.14"></a> When the environ has neither key, the request has no target to report: the callable logs an error that names `RAW_URI` and `REQUEST_URI`, and answers the plain 500 of HY-60 before it calls `start_response`.
  - <a id="HY-100.15"></a> Python ASGI: `create_asgi(app, sessions, files=None, around=None, written=None)` of the package `polyspec.hyper` of the Python server `polyspec-hyper` takes the arguments of `create_server` (HY-97, HY-99) and returns an ASGI 3 application callable that an ASGI server runs. <a id="HY-100.16"></a> The callable answers every request of the scope type `http` as `create_server` does: the public files before `around`, the request body read up to the body limit of the application and no more (HY-59), the session cookie of a new session first (HY-45) and the request hook `around` (HY-97). <a id="HY-100.17"></a> It runs the pipeline of a request in a worker thread, so the event loop of the server answers other requests while a request responds. <a id="HY-100.18"></a> It sends one `http.response.start` with the status and the headers of the `Response` and one `http.response.body` with the complete body: the write hook `written` (HY-99) reports that the write ended when both sends return, and that it failed when a send raises, which an ASGI server does for a connection that the client closed; when the write failed, the callable calls `written`, then the disconnect hook (HY-67) with the request that it gave to `around` and the reply of the last call of `answer`, and lets the error propagate to the server. <a id="HY-100.19"></a> A cancellation of the task reports `written` with `ended` false and propagates the cancellation, without the disconnect hook, because the cancellation does not state that the client closed the connection. <a id="HY-100.20"></a> As `create_server` does (HY-67), the callable learns of a closed connection only when a send fails; it does not watch the `http.disconnect` message. <a id="HY-100.21"></a> The hook is not called for the files of the public directory. <a id="HY-100.22"></a> The library names no server; a deployment runs the callable with the server that it chooses. <a id="HY-100.23"></a> The request path is `scope['raw_path']` decoded as latin-1: the raw bytes of the target path without the query, which the ASGI specification defines; it is split as HY-42 splits a target. <a id="HY-100.24"></a> The raw query is `scope['query_string']` decoded as latin-1 (HY-56). <a id="HY-100.25"></a> The callable never builds the path from `scope['path']`, which the server has percent-decoded. <a id="HY-100.26"></a> An ASGI server that omits `raw_path`, which the specification makes optional, makes the request have no target to report: the callable logs an error that names `raw_path`, and sends the plain 500 of HY-60 before it sends anything. <a id="HY-100.27"></a> When a send of that 500 fails, the callable calls `written` with the failed write and lets the error propagate to the server, as HY-67 does for a failed send.
  - <a id="HY-100.28"></a> Node: `listener(app, sessions, options)` of the Node server returns the `node:http` request listener that `server` installs. <a id="HY-100.29"></a> The listener returns a promise that settles after the write hook and the disconnect hook of the request have run (HY-99).
  - <a id="HY-100.30"></a> PHP: `run` is the entry of the front controller; it turns `ignore_user_abort` off, registers the shutdown function that calls the write hook and the disconnect hook (HY-67, HY-99), and writes the plain 500 of an uncaught exception or a fatal error (HY-60).

## Errors

- **HY-132** <a id="HY-132.1"></a> Every failure that hyper raises is an error with a kind that never changes, an HTTP status or none, and a category, and a caller tells failures apart by the kind and never by the class or the message. <a id="HY-132.2"></a> In each runtime the error is of the class of its category, `HyperValueError`, `HyperTypeError`, `HyperIoError`, `HyperStoreError`, `HyperBusyError` or `HyperInternalError`, which extends the base class of that category (PHP `InvalidArgumentException`, `TypeError` and `RuntimeException`; Python `ValueError`, `TypeError`, `OSError` and `RuntimeError`; Node `RangeError`, `TypeError` and `Error`), and it gives its kind and its status as PHP `kind()` and `status()` and as the properties `kind` and `status` in Python and Node. <a id="HY-132.3"></a> The kinds of hyper are those of the table below, and an error of a library that hyper uses, such as http-form, http-negotiation, http-media-type, http-cookie, json, the template data model, the session-store library or the binding, reaches the caller with the kind, the status and the category of that library, in the class of that category of hyper. <a id="HY-132.4"></a> A message that a rule states is the message of the error in every runtime, with no prefix of a runtime, and no case compares a message that no rule states. <a id="HY-132.5"></a> The only failures without a kind are the argument errors of HY-106.8 and HY-106.16, which the runtime raises in its own class, and an exception that code of the application raises, such as a handler, a hook or a session store, reaches the caller as it was raised and is no error of hyper. <a id="HY-132.6"></a> A broken invariant of the core is kind `internal`, a panic of the core included, and a request that meets it fails with HY-43.

  | Kind | Status | Category | Rule |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `invalid_application` | none | `value` | HY-106.21 |
  | `invalid_build` | none | `value` | HY-106.21 |
  | `not_application_path` | none | `value` | HY-46.3 |
  | `not_redirect_result` | none | `value` | HY-50.3 |
  | `page_status_not_allowed` | none | `value` | HY-58.6 |
  | `reply_status_not_allowed` | none | `value` | HY-69.9 |
  | `cookie_name_not_allowed` | none | `value` | HY-52.16 |
  | `cookie_value_not_allowed` | none | `value` | HY-52.16 |
  | `negative_max_age` | none | `value` | HY-52.16 |
  | `cache_control_not_allowed` | none | `value` | HY-52.16, HY-122.6 |
  | `cache_control_shared` | none | `value` | HY-52.16, HY-122.6 |
  | `referrer_policy_not_allowed` | none | `value` | HY-103.9 |
  | `invalid_csrf_form` | none | `value` | HY-24.14 |
  | `malformed_json` | none | `value` | HY-54.21 |
  | `not_selected` | none | `type` | HY-116.21 |
  | `invalid_session_token` | none | `store` | HY-24.14 |
  | `invalid_session_record` | none | `store` | HY-104.23 |
  | `shared_holds_context` | none | `value` | HY-124.8 |
  | `invalid_representation` | none | `value` | HY-122.2 to HY-122.8 |
  | `integer_range` | none | `value` | HY-52.18, HY-69.9 |
  | `internal` | none | `internal` | HY-132.6 |

- **HY-27** <a id="HY-27.1"></a> A path without a route, or a loader that reports a missing resource, responds with status 404. <a id="HY-27.2"></a> A method other than `GET`, `HEAD` or a declared `POST` responds with status 405; a representation checks the method of HY-121 instead. <a id="HY-27.3"></a> A loader or an action reports a missing resource with the not-found stop, whose message is `not found`; the forbidden stop of HY-51 has the message `forbidden` and the bad-request stop of HY-58 the message `bad request`. <a id="HY-27.4"></a> The server answers a `HEAD` request as the `GET` request of the same target (RFC 9110, section 9.3.2): every step runs with the request method `GET`, so a handler reads `GET`, and `App.handle` returns the `GET` response with its body, which the response hook (HY-60), the response limit (HY-66) and `around` (HY-97) receive with the request as the host gave it. <a id="HY-27.5"></a> The host writes the status and the headers of the response to a `HEAD` request, with the `Content-Length` of its body unless the status is 204 or 304, and no body. <a id="HY-27.6"></a> Every 405 has the header `Allow` (RFC 9110, section 15.5.6): `GET, HEAD` for a route, `GET, HEAD, POST` for a route that declares `post`, `GET, HEAD` for the 405 of HY-62.23, `POST` for `/_hyper/keep` (HY-40), and the methods of HY-121.6 for a representation.

- **HY-50** <a id="HY-50.1"></a> A loader or an action may stop the request with a redirect: it throws the redirect of a result of HY-25, which names an application path (HY-46) and may carry flash values and changed topics. <a id="HY-50.2"></a> The server responds with status 303 and `Location` with the base path, stores the flash values and the changed topics as HY-25 does, and renders nothing. <a id="HY-50.3"></a> Making a redirect stop of a result that is not a redirect fails with the error `a redirect stop needs a redirect result (HY-50)`, of the classes of HY-46.3; the message of a redirect stop is `redirect to` followed by a space and its location.

- **HY-51** <a id="HY-51.1"></a> A loader or an action may stop the request as forbidden. <a id="HY-51.2"></a> The server responds with status 403 and the text `Forbidden`, and runs no other loader or action of the request.

- **HY-52** <a id="HY-52.1"></a> Every loader and action of a request may receive the reply of the request. <a id="HY-52.2"></a> The reply adds a cookie with a name of `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*` that does not start with `hy-`, a value of the characters `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ ~ -` and an optional `Max-Age`, or removes a cookie with `Max-Age=0`. <a id="HY-52.13"></a> Each such cookie is written by `set_cookie` of http-cookie with its `Max-Age`, the path `/`, `secure` under the conditions of HY-45, `http_only` and `same_site` `Lax`, so its field value is `<name>=<value>`, then `; Max-Age=<seconds>` when it has one, `; Path=/`, `; Secure` under those conditions, `; HttpOnly` and `; SameSite=Lax` (CK-9). <a id="HY-52.4"></a> Another name or value fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-52.5"></a> A page response has `Cache-Control: no-store`; the reply may set the `Cache-Control` of a page response with status 200, and its value replaces `no-store`. <a id="HY-52.6"></a> A page carries the session token of its visitor (HY-10, HY-24), so a value without the directive `private` or `no-store`, or with `public` or `s-maxage`, fails with HY-43: a shared cache must not give the page of one visitor to another. <a id="HY-52.7"></a> The server session adds only its cookie to a response, and no caching header. <a id="HY-52.8"></a> A response without a body, a 304 of HY-53 included, has no `Content-Type`. <a id="HY-52.9"></a> The response of the request contains the cookies of its reply, whether it is a page, a redirect or a failure of HY-27, HY-50 or HY-51. <a id="HY-52.18"></a> A `Max-Age` is an integer of the data model that is not negative: a value that the binding does not take as an integer, such as a float in PHP and Python, a bool, a string or a Node number outside the safe integers, fails with kind `invalid_number` of the binding (B-2), and an integer outside ±(2^53 − 1), which PHP and Python can give, fails with kind `integer_range` of hyper before its sign is checked. <a id="HY-52.15"></a> A cookie name, a cookie value or a `Cache-Control` value that is not a string fails with kind `invalid_argument_type` of the binding before hyper reads it, so the types of a cookie are checked before its values. <a id="HY-52.16"></a> A cookie of these types fails otherwise with kind `cookie_name_not_allowed` and the message `cookie name <name> is not allowed (HY-52)`, `cookie_value_not_allowed` and `cookie value of <name> has a character that is not allowed (HY-52)` or `negative_max_age` and `cookie <name> has a negative Max-Age (HY-52)` in this order, and a `Cache-Control` string with kind `cache_control_not_allowed` and the message `Cache-Control has a character that is not allowed (HY-52)` or `cache_control_shared` and `Cache-Control <value> lets a shared cache store the page; it needs private or no-store and neither public nor s-maxage (HY-52)`, where `<name>` and `<value>` are the given strings.

- **HY-105** <a id="HY-105.1"></a> Loaders, actions and representation handlers (HY-121) receive the services that the application binds. <a id="HY-105.2"></a> The application binds a factory for a service; the server calls the factory on the first use of the service and gives the same service to every later handler of the application. <a id="HY-105.3"></a> A service without a factory fails the request with HY-43. <a id="HY-105.4"></a> A handler names a service by the class of a parameter in PHP and Python, and by the key that it passes to `services.get` in Node.
