- **HY-107** <a id="HY-107.1"></a> A loader or an action may let an error of the ORM escape, and the server answers it as the stop of its meaning, so that a handler calls the ORM directly. <a id="HY-107.7"></a> The server recognizes an error of the ORM by the error classes of the orm package and by its kind, so hyper depends on the orm package, and the kinds `no_rows` and `revision_changed` are kinds that the orm library states. <a id="HY-107.8"></a> The kind `no_rows`, a strict query for one row that matched no row, is answered as `NotFound` (HY-27: status 404 and the text `Not Found`). <a id="HY-107.9"></a> The kind `revision_changed`, a write with an expected revision that found the row at another revision or no row, is answered, when an action raises it, as the page of the route with status 409 and no data of its own (HY-58); a loader that raises it fails with HY-43, because the page cannot load. <a id="HY-107.5"></a> Every other error of the ORM, and every error of another kind, is not handled by this rule and fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-107.6"></a> A handler that wants another answer catches the error itself.

- **HY-53** <a id="HY-53.1"></a> A JSON response with status 200 has a weak `ETag`, `W/"<digits>"`, made of the first 32 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 digest of its body after every occurrence of the masked token of the response is replaced by the session token (HY-24). <a id="HY-53.2"></a> Two responses with the same data and the same session token therefore have the same tag although their masks differ, and the tag is weak because their bytes differ (RFC 9110, section 8.8.1). <a id="HY-53.3"></a> A renewed session (HY-72) has another token and so another tag. <a id="HY-53.4"></a> A `GET` request whose `If-None-Match` header equals that tag receives status 304 with the headers of the 200 response except `Content-Type` and no body, because a 304 carries no representation (RFC 9110, section 15.4.5) and php-fpm removes the `Content-Type` of a 304; an action runs whatever tag its request names.

- **HY-103** <a id="HY-103.1"></a> A loader or an action may set the `Referrer-Policy` of the page and JSON answers of its request with `Reply::referrerPolicy(value)` in PHP, `reply.referrerPolicy(value)` in Node and `reply.referrer_policy(value)` in Python. <a id="HY-103.2"></a> The value is one of the tokens of the Referrer-Policy specification, compared exactly: `no-referrer`, `no-referrer-when-downgrade`, `origin`, `origin-when-cross-origin`, `same-origin`, `strict-origin`, `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and `unsafe-url`. <a id="HY-103.3"></a> Another value fails with HY-43, as a `Cache-Control` value without `private` or `no-store` does (HY-52). <a id="HY-103.4"></a> A later call replaces the value. <a id="HY-103.5"></a> Every page and JSON answer of the request, whatever its status, then has the header `Referrer-Policy` with that value, and so does a 304 of HY-53. <a id="HY-103.6"></a> Without such a call a page or JSON answer has no `Referrer-Policy` from the reply. <a id="HY-103.7"></a> The method sets no other header, and the redirects, the stops and the plain text failures of HY-27, HY-50, HY-51 and HY-65 have none from the reply. <a id="HY-103.9"></a> A value that is not a string fails with kind `invalid_argument_type` of the binding, and another string fails with kind `referrer_policy_not_allowed` and the message `Referrer-Policy <value> is not a token of the Referrer-Policy specification (HY-103)`.

- **HY-104** <a id="HY-104.1"></a> The PHP, Node and Python servers that share one session directory share its sessions, and so do the processes of one server. <a id="HY-104.25"></a> The storage of a session, which is its identifier, its record bytes, its lock, its file or Redis key and its expiry, is the rule of the session-store library, and hyper uses its store interface; the session values that hyper keeps in a record, which are the token (HY-24), the flash values and the changed topics (HY-25), the kept values (HY-40), the conversion between a record and the data model (HY-104.13, HY-104.14) and the keys of HY-104.22 and HY-104.23, are rules of hyper. <a id="HY-104.2"></a> A session is the file `sess_<id>` of the directory, the form of the files handler of PHP: its bytes are the record of its values in the form `php_serialize` of PHP, read and written with `@polyspec/php-serialization` and `polyspec-php-serialization`, its mode is 0600, and a file without bytes is an empty session. <a id="HY-104.3"></a> The requests of one session run one after another in every process and no write is lost: each server holds `flock` with `LOCK_EX` on the session file from the opening of the session of a request to its closing, and a representation request, which opens no session (HY-120), holds no lock, and the operating system releases the lock of a process that ended. <a id="HY-104.26"></a> The PHP server keeps a session with the file store of the session-store library, as the Node and Python servers do, and not with the native session handler of PHP, with which it shares only the file name, the record form `php_serialize`, the file mode and `flock` with `LOCK_EX`. <a id="HY-104.27"></a> Every server waits for the lock of a session file in the core of the session-store library, which blocks on `flock` with `LOCK_EX` on a thread of its own for each waiting session, with no retry and no interval, so the operating system orders the waiting requests as it orders the native files handler of PHP. <a id="HY-104.7"></a> The server writes a record over the file in place under the lock and cuts the file to its length, as PHP does, so a process that ends during a write can leave a record that the next request cannot read; a request that changed nothing keeps the bytes and sets a new modification time. <a id="HY-104.8"></a> Only a missing session file starts a new session: a session file that the server cannot read or decode fails the request with its error (HY-60). <a id="HY-104.31"></a> An identifier is 22 to 256 characters of `A-Za-z0-9,-`, the identifiers that PHP creates for its session handlers (`session.sid_length` from 22 to 256), as SE-5.1 of the session-store library states: every server creates 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits (SE-5.3) and accepts the identifier of another and of a PHP peer. <a id="HY-104.10"></a> An identifier without a file names no session and creates no file. <a id="HY-104.11"></a> A renewal (HY-72) creates the new file before it removes the old one, and a request that waited for the lock of a removed file starts a new session. <a id="HY-104.12"></a> A value that a request did not set stays as it was read. <a id="HY-104.13"></a> A Node or Python server reads a record as the data model: an integer key is its decimal text, a float its number, a `stdClass` a map and a reference its value, and a list where the session keeps a map is that map, because a PHP array with the keys 0 to n-1 reads as a list. <a id="HY-104.14"></a> It writes an empty map and a map with the keys 0 to n-1 as a `stdClass`, so that every server reads it as a map; a record that holds an object of another class fails the request. <a id="HY-104.34"></a> It writes a number of the data model that is an integer within ±(2^53 − 1) as a PHP integer and every other number as a PHP float, so that a PHP peer reads an integer as an integer; the integer is read from the bits of the number without a rounding conversion. <a id="HY-104.15"></a> The removal of expired sessions skips a session whose lock a request holds. <a id="HY-104.33"></a> No server removes expired sessions while it answers a request: the application calls `collect` of its store (SF-5) when it chooses, such as from a scheduled task, because a removal during a request would make the time of an answer depend on the number of session files and, done by chance as PHP does with `session.gc_probability`, the result of a check depend on chance (HR-89), and a PHP peer that shares the directory removes expired files by its own settings. <a id="HY-104.28"></a> `tests/scripts/session-shared.test.mts` checks it with several processes of each of the three servers on one session. <a id="HY-104.29"></a> The requests of one session in one process wait in a queue of that process before they wait for the lock of the session, and a request that leaves before its turn, such as one whose connection closed (HY-67), leaves the queue, and one that leaves while it waits for the lock releases the lock as soon as it holds it. <a id="HY-104.32"></a> A session store of files takes an existing absolute directory and a lifetime, an unsigned integer of seconds whose default is 1440, and making it with another directory or a lifetime of 0 fails with the kind of the session-store library (`invalid_directory`, `invalid_lifetime`). <a id="HY-104.20"></a> A record whose value is no array fails as a record that cannot be decoded does. <a id="HY-104.21"></a> A session file whose modification time is older than the lifetime names no session: a request with its identifier starts a new session, and the removal of expired sessions removes the file. <a id="HY-104.22"></a> A session holds the token under `_hyper_csrf`, the flash values and the changed topics under `_hyper_flash` as a map with `values` and `changed`, and the kept values under `_hyper_keep` as a map from a region name to a map from a path to its value. <a id="HY-104.23"></a> A stored flash value or kept value of another form fails the request with HY-43, and no server repairs it. <a id="HY-104.35"></a> The kept values of every region are checked when the session reads them, for a read of one region and for a write, so a stored region of another form fails every read and write of the kept values. <a id="HY-104.30"></a> A session store returns null for a key that holds no value, replaces the value of a key that is set again, and removes a key without failing when it holds none; a store that an application writes in its own language implements this interface, its locking and its sharing with other processes are the task of the application, and an exception that it raises reaches the caller of `App.handle` as it was raised.

- **HY-115** <a id="HY-115.1"></a> The PHP, Node and Python servers that share one Redis server share its sessions, with the protocol of phpredis 6.3.0, and so do the processes of one server. <a id="HY-115.2"></a> A session is the key `PHPREDIS_SESSION:<id>`, whose bytes are the record of HY-104 and which expires after the lifetime of the session. <a id="HY-115.3"></a> The requests of one session run one after another in every process: a request takes the lock `<key>_LOCK` with `SET NX PX`, tries it again after a pause while another holds it, and fails with status 500 (HY-43) when its tries end, in every server and whatever `error_reporting` keeps. <a id="HY-115.4"></a> A request that opens a session reads it after it holds the lock, and one whose key is gone by then starts a new session. <a id="HY-115.5"></a> A lock expires so that a process that ended cannot hold it for ever, so a holder compares the value of the lock with its own secret before it writes with `SETEX`: a request that lost its lock writes nothing. <a id="HY-115.23"></a> Every server closes the session before it answers, so a request that lost its lock fails with status 500 (HY-43) in the three servers. <a id="HY-115.7"></a> A request that changed nothing keeps the bytes and sets a new expiry with `EXPIRE` without comparing the lock, because it writes no record, so a long request that only reads does not fail when its lock expires. <a id="HY-115.8"></a> A request releases its lock with the script that compares the value and deletes the key, so it never releases the lock of another. <a id="HY-115.24"></a> A phpredis peer shares the sessions of a server when it runs with `redis.session.locking_enabled=1`, a `redis.session.lock_expire` other than 0, a `redis.session.lock_retries` other than -1, `redis.session.lock_failure_readonly=0`, `redis.session.early_refresh=0`, `redis.session.compression=none` and `session.serialize_handler=php_serialize`, and with the lock wait of the server converted to the microseconds of `redis.session.lock_wait_time`; with another setting the sessions are not shared. <a id="HY-115.29"></a> Every server takes the connection settings of the Redis store, which are the addresses, TLS and the ACL user, and not a client of the application, and the options `lockExpire` in seconds, `lockRetries` and `lockWait` in microseconds, which are `redis.session.lock_expire`, `redis.session.lock_retries` and `redis.session.lock_wait_time` of phpredis; every server of one Redis server gives them the same values, and the expiry is longer than any request. <a id="HY-115.11"></a> A renewal (HY-72) writes the new key before it deletes the old one, and the rules of identifiers and values of HY-104 hold. <a id="HY-115.12"></a> A request that cannot reach the Redis server answers status 500 (HY-43) in every server, tells no detail and sets no session cookie, so the client keeps its session, and the sessions that the Redis server kept go on after it starts again; a process that ended while it held a lock delays the requests of that session until the lock expires and wrote nothing. <a id="HY-115.13"></a> `tests/scripts/session-shared-redis.test.mts` checks it with processes of the three servers on a real Redis server, the PHP server through real phpredis, and `tests/scripts/session-redis-failure.test.mts` with a lock that really expires, a killed process, the HTTP servers of the board and a stop and a start of the Redis server. <a id="HY-115.26"></a> On a primary with replicas, every server asks Redis Sentinel for the primary before the first command of each request that has a session, also on a connection that it keeps, because a connection to a former primary accepts writes for some seconds after a promotion. <a id="HY-115.16"></a> A request answers status 500 (HY-43) while no primary answers and the session goes on after a promotion; a failover keeps what a replica acknowledged and can lose what it did not receive, because replication is asynchronous. <a id="HY-115.17"></a> The connections take TLS and an ACL user in every server. <a id="HY-115.18"></a> `tests/scripts/session-redis-failover.test.mts` checks them with real Redis servers and Sentinels. <a id="HY-115.27"></a> On Redis Cluster every command of the protocol has one key, so a session and its lock can live on different primaries, and every server speaks the protocol through a cluster connection; the `rediscluster` handler of phpredis takes no lock, so a phpredis peer does not share the sessions of a cluster. <a id="HY-115.20"></a> `tests/scripts/session-redis-cluster.test.mts` checks it on a real cluster of three primaries, also while a slot moves. <a id="HY-115.28"></a> `lifetime` of the Redis store is an unsigned integer of seconds with the default 1440, and `lockExpire` is an unsigned integer of seconds that the caller states, with no default, because no value is longer than every request of every application; a lifetime or a lock expiry of 0 fails with the kind of the session-store library (`invalid_lifetime`, `invalid_lock_expire`). <a id="HY-115.22"></a> A request tries the lock once and then `lockRetries` more times.

- **HY-58** <a id="HY-58.1"></a> A loader or an action may stop the request as a bad request. <a id="HY-58.2"></a> The server responds with status 400 and the text `Bad Request`, and runs no other loader or action of the request. <a id="HY-58.3"></a> An action may also return the route page with a stated status of 200, 409 or 422 and data: the server renders the route page with the route data merged with that data, as JSON for a JSON request and as a document otherwise, and responds with that status. <a id="HY-58.4"></a> Another status fails with HY-43. <a id="HY-58.5"></a> HY-26 is the page with status 422; a page with status 200 follows HY-52 and HY-53. <a id="HY-58.6"></a> Making a page with another status fails with the error `a page status`, a space, the status and ` is not 200, 409 or 422 (HY-58)`, of the classes of HY-46.3.

- **HY-69** <a id="HY-69.1"></a> A loader or an action may give the page of its request the status 403 with `Reply::status(403)` in PHP and `reply.status(403)` in Node and Python, for a page that shows other data in place of the data that the request may not see, such as a sign-in form in place of a page that needs a session. <a id="HY-69.2"></a> A page response that has status 200 otherwise, the page of a `GET` request or an action result page with status 200 (HY-58), then has status 403 and is rendered as it is with 200, as JSON for a JSON request and as a document otherwise. <a id="HY-69.3"></a> As every response with status 400 or more it has `Cache-Control: no-store` (HY-65), and as every response with another status than 200 it has no `ETag` and never receives 304 (HY-53). <a id="HY-69.4"></a> A page with status 409 or 422, a redirect, a stop and a failure keep their own status. <a id="HY-69.5"></a> Another status fails with HY-43, because 403 states that the request may not see the page; 401 would require a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge (RFC 9110), and 200 would state that the response is the page. <a id="HY-69.9"></a> A status that the binding does not take as an integer fails with kind `invalid_number` of the binding (B-2), an integer outside ±(2^53 − 1) fails with kind `integer_range` of hyper, and another integer fails with kind `reply_status_not_allowed` and the message `page status <status> of a reply is not 403 (HY-69)`, where `<status>` is the integer in decimal digits.

- **HY-59** <a id="HY-59.1"></a> The application declares a body limit, the largest request body in bytes (8 MiB by default), and its form types, the media types of the request bodies that its actions and `/_hyper/keep` accept: one or both of `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `multipart/form-data`, by default `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. <a id="HY-59.2"></a> Another limit or form type fails when the application opens. <a id="HY-59.3"></a> The server checks a request in this order, and runs no loader or action when a check fails:

  1. <a id="HY-59.4"></a> A body larger than the limit receives status 413 with the text `Content Too Large`, for every request and before HY-42. <a id="HY-59.5"></a> The size of a body is its length, or its `Content-Length` when that is larger, because PHP leaves the body empty when it is larger than `post_max_size`. <a id="HY-59.6"></a> Every server stops reading a body when it passes the body limit or another limit of HY-131.11.
  2. <a id="HY-59.12"></a> After routing and HY-27, a `POST` request to an action or to `/_hyper/keep` whose `Content-Type` is no media type, the empty value included, receives status 400 with the text `Bad Request`, as F-12 of http-form reads it with MT-4 of http-media-type (kind `malformed_content_type`), and one whose media type, its type and subtype without parameters, is not a form type receives status 415 with the text `Unsupported Media Type`.
  3. <a id="HY-59.8"></a> Then the CSRF check of HY-24 answers 403.

  <a id="HY-59.9"></a> `run` of PHP fails before it answers when `post_max_size` is smaller than the limit, when `multipart/form-data` is a form type and `enable_post_data_reading` is on (HY-57), or when `enable_post_data_reading` is on under a SAPI that serves requests, every SAPI but `cli` and `phpdbg`, because PHP then reads every request body with its own reader before the application runs. <a id="HY-59.10"></a> Every host reads a body that the request sends in chunks, and the body limit applies to it. <a id="HY-59.13"></a> `mediaType()` of the request returns the type and subtype of its `Content-Type` in lower case without parameters, as F-12 of http-form reads them, the empty text for a request without `Content-Type`, and fails with kind `malformed_content_type` (status 400) for a `Content-Type` that is no media type.

- **HY-60** <a id="HY-60.1"></a> The application may declare a response hook. <a id="HY-60.2"></a> The server calls it once for every response of the application with the request, the response and the elapsed time in milliseconds, including the responses that hyper answers itself: 400 (HY-42, HY-58), 403 (HY-24, HY-51), 404 and 405 (HY-27), 406 and the static shell (HY-62), the 400 and 406 of HY-116, the 400 of HY-127, the 400, 405 and 415 of HY-121, 413 and 415 (HY-59), and 500 (HY-43, HY-66). <a id="HY-60.3"></a> The request is the request as received, with the base path. <a id="HY-60.4"></a> The response is the response of the application with its `Content-Security-Policy` (HY-45); the session cookie that the session adds afterwards is not part of it. <a id="HY-60.5"></a> The elapsed time counts on a monotonic clock from the start of the request: `run` and `handle` of PHP take the start from their caller as an `hrtime(true)` value, such as the value that the first statement of a front controller takes, or count from their own call; the Node server counts with `performance.now()` from the time when `node:http` gives the request. <a id="HY-60.6"></a> No server subtracts a wall clock time such as `REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT` or `microtime(true)`, because an adjustment of the system time moves the wall clock backwards and gives a negative elapsed time. <a id="HY-60.7"></a> The Node server also reports the 400 and 431 responses to requests that `node:http` cannot parse, with a request of the method and the target of the request line, or with no request when the packet has no request line. <a id="HY-60.8"></a> The hook also receives the reply of the request (HY-52), so that it reads the values that the loaders and actions of the request decided: the reply that they received, also when the request ended with a stop (HY-50, HY-51, HY-58), a failure of HY-27 or an error of HY-43, and a new empty reply when the server answered before routing (HY-42, HY-59, a path without a route, `/_hyper/keep` and the responses that `node:http` cannot give to the application) or without a loader or an action (the 405 and 406 responses and the shell of HY-62, the 406 of HY-116 and every response of a representation, HY-121 and HY-122). <a id="HY-60.9"></a> A loader or an action records such a value with a note of the reply, a name and any value; a later note of the same name replaces the value and keeps its position. <a id="HY-60.10"></a> The server does not read the notes, and they are not part of the response. <a id="HY-60.11"></a> The hook also receives the failure of a 500 of HY-43 or HY-66, so that an application writes the cause with its own line: the message of the error of HY-43 (the message of a PHP `Throwable` or of a Node `Error`, or the text of another thrown value) or `the response to <method> <path> has <size> bytes, more than the response limit of <limit> bytes` of HY-66; for every other response it receives null. <a id="HY-60.12"></a> The files of the public directory of the Node server are not responses of the application. <a id="HY-60.13"></a> An error that the hook throws is not handled by HY-43; it reaches the caller of `handle`.

  - <a id="HY-60.14"></a> An error that escapes the answer of a request, because HY-43 does not handle it, is a failed read of the body, a failed stat of a file of the public directory, a failed session open or close, a failed write of the response, an error that the response hook throws, or an error that `around` raises outside `answer` (HY-97). <a id="HY-60.15"></a> The server logs it with the message of HY-43 and answers a plain 500 that hyper writes itself, identical in every adapter: status 500, the text `Internal Server Error`, `Cache-Control: no-store` (HY-65) and `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors <policy>` (HY-45). <a id="HY-60.16"></a> No server reports that 500 to the response hook. <a id="HY-60.17"></a> The write hook (HY-99) receives it once, with the request as the server received it. <a id="HY-60.18"></a> The request as received has the target, the headers and the cookies of the request; a body that was not read is empty, and its size is the Content-Length that the client declared. <a id="HY-60.19"></a> A request whose target the transport does not give (a WSGI environ without `RAW_URI` and `REQUEST_URI`, or an ASGI scope without `raw_path`) has no request to report, so no hook receives its 500. <a id="HY-60.20"></a> The 500 is written only when the response has not started. <a id="HY-60.21"></a> When the response has started, or the write of the 500 fails, the server closes the connection; a write that fails is reported to the write hook once, so no hook is called twice for a request. <a id="HY-60.22"></a> The WSGI and ASGI callables (HY-100) write the same 500 before their `start_response` or their first send. <a id="HY-60.23"></a> `run` writes the same 500 for an uncaught exception, through `set_exception_handler`, and for a fatal error of the request, which the shutdown function reads from `error_get_last()` as E_ERROR, E_CORE_ERROR, E_COMPILE_ERROR or E_USER_ERROR (a memory or time limit is an E_ERROR), when headers have not been sent.
  - <a id="HY-60.24"></a> The plain 500 of an escaped error keeps the response headers that the caller of hyper set before hyper received the request, and no other header. <a id="HY-60.25"></a> PHP keeps the headers of `headers_list()` at the call of `run`, and `sendReplacing` removes every other header and adds them again before the headers of the 500. <a id="HY-60.26"></a> Node writes the 500 with `writeHead` on the `node:http` response, which keeps a header that the caller set with `setHeader` before the listener of hyper ran. <a id="HY-60.27"></a> The WSGI and ASGI callables (HY-100) pass the 500 to the `start_response` or the `send` of their caller as any response.

  <a id="HY-60.32"></a> A note name that is not a string fails with kind `invalid_argument_type` of the binding. <a id="HY-60.29"></a> `notes()` returns the notes as a list of pairs of a name, which stays a string also when it is decimal, and its value, in the order of the first note of each name, in the three servers. <a id="HY-60.30"></a> The `http.server` server has no caller before it, so its plain 500 keeps no header of a caller. <a id="HY-60.31"></a> `handle` of every server takes the start of the request as an optional value of its monotonic clock, `hrtime(true)` in PHP, `performance.now()` in Node and `time.perf_counter_ns()` in Python, and counts from its own call without it.

- **HY-65** <a id="HY-65.1"></a> Every response with a status of 400 or more has `Cache-Control: no-store`, so that no cache stores a failure: the plain text responses of HY-24, HY-27, HY-40, HY-42, HY-43, HY-51, HY-58, HY-59, HY-62, HY-66, HY-116, HY-127 and HY-121, the responses of a representation handler with such a status (HY-122), the plain 500 of an escaped error (HY-60), the 400 and 431 responses of the Node server to requests that `node:http` cannot parse (HY-60), the pages with status 409 or 422 (HY-58) and the pages with status 403 (HY-69). <a id="HY-65.2"></a> A reply does not change it (HY-52). <a id="HY-65.3"></a> Without the header, a cache may store a 404 or 405 response by its heuristic freshness (RFC 9111).

- **HY-66** <a id="HY-66.1"></a> The application declares a response limit, the largest response body in bytes (8 MiB by default); a limit that is not a positive integer fails when the application opens. <a id="HY-66.2"></a> The limit bounds the body that the server holds for sending one response, which a slow client keeps in the memory of the server process and of a web server that buffers the response. <a id="HY-66.3"></a> A response whose body is larger than the limit is not sent: the server writes `hyper: the response to <method> <path> has <size> bytes, more than the response limit of <limit> bytes` to its log, answers status 500 with the text `Internal Server Error` as HY-43 does, and reports that 500 to the response hook (HY-60) with the reply of the request. <a id="HY-66.4"></a> The size of a body is its length in bytes. <a id="HY-66.5"></a> The server renders a body completely before it compares its size, because the template programs render a document to one string.

- **HY-67** <a id="HY-67.1"></a> The application may declare a disconnect hook. <a id="HY-67.2"></a> The server calls it once, with the request as received, the elapsed milliseconds (HY-60) and the reply of the request, for a request whose client closed the connection before it received the complete response. <a id="HY-67.13"></a> A disconnect hook that is not callable fails when the application opens, in Node and Python; PHP refuses it by the type of its parameter.

  - <a id="HY-67.3"></a> The Node server learns of the close when `node:http` reports that the connection closed before the response was written. <a id="HY-67.4"></a> It then runs no further loader, action or rendering of the request after the one that is running, writes no response, does not call the response hook and calls the disconnect hook.
  - <a id="HY-67.5"></a> PHP reports a closed connection only when a write to it fails, and a write of a small response to a closed connection can succeed. <a id="HY-67.6"></a> `run` turns `ignore_user_abort` off, so PHP ends the script at the first failed write of the response, and a shutdown function calls the disconnect hook when `connection_aborted()` is 1. <a id="HY-67.7"></a> The PHP server therefore renders the complete response and calls the response hook (HY-60) before it can detect the close, and it does not detect a close when every write of the response succeeds.
  - <a id="HY-67.8"></a> The Python server of `polyspec-hyper` (`create_server` of `polyspec.hyper`) learns of a closed connection only when a write of the response fails, as PHP does: `http.server` raises `BrokenPipeError`, `ConnectionResetError` or `ConnectionAbortedError` for a write to a connection that the client closed. <a id="HY-67.9"></a> The server renders the complete response and calls the response hook (HY-60) first, then writes the response; when a write fails with one of these errors, it writes no more of the response and calls the disconnect hook once with the request as received, the elapsed milliseconds and the reply of the request. <a id="HY-67.10"></a> It counts the elapsed time with `time.perf_counter_ns()`, a monotonic clock, from the time when its request handler starts the request, as it does for the response hook. <a id="HY-67.11"></a> It does not detect a close when every write of the response succeeds. <a id="HY-67.12"></a> `App.respond` answers a request as `App.handle` does and returns the response with the reply of the request, so that the server holds the reply that the disconnect hook receives; `App.handle` returns only the response.

- **HYC-9** <a id="HYC-9.1"></a> An error in the browser code is thrown from the htmx response hook. <a id="HYC-9.2"></a> htmx reports it with the `htmx:error` event and does not swap.

## Implementation equivalence

PHP, Python and TypeScript must satisfy the same declared protocol units, including manifest, request and file-limit rules (HY-1, HY-27, HY-114). CI runs declaration validation and cross-language equivalence in the entry `gates` of `ci.yml`, independently of language-specific, rendering and browser jobs. Each parity target runs exactly once; a failed parity target fails the entry `gates`, and so `ci-passed`, which a release requires of its run.

Each CI group owns its pinned tools, locked dependencies and build inputs. Language jobs install only the environments they execute. The protocol parity and browser integration groups independently prepare all implementations they compare and never consume another language job’s installation or build artifacts. Tool selection uses the shared `make install-tools TOOLS="..."` interface; package installation stays with npm, Composer and uv. Installation may download locked inputs; builds and checks remain offline. The selected installer is supplied by the pinned Kit release. npm is prepared by its separate bootstrap selector; PHP symbol extractors are installed explicitly through `make kit-install-symbols EXTRACTORS="php"` in the groups that execute them.

## Interface terms

A string is a text. A number is a number of the data model (VAL-2). A boolean is `true` or `false`. Null is the value `null`. A bigint is an integer of arbitrary size. Bytes is a byte sequence. A value is any value of the data model of HY-54. None is no result.
